types.name: AccruedTimeEntry
types.description:
Singular Accrued Time Entry Event 
Each entry has information about accrued time for a worker in a particular location

4 primary examples include the following: 
A worker accruing x millis of SICK of time 
A worker withdrawing x millis of SICK time for use on a particular date 
A worker canceling a previous withdrawn time 
A withdrawal that has been paid out to the worker

Date that a withdrawal will take place

This is set to null for accrue/cancellation/paid entries

-WITHDRAWAL represents them claiming it for a particular date
-WITHDRAWAL_CANCELED represents a cancellation of a previous withdrawal record

-ROLLOVER represents the balance rollover between calendar years

types.name: AnalyticsDimension
types.description:
A dimension is a categorical or descriptive attribute of data,
typically qualitative, that provides context for analysis. It represents
the "who," "what," "where," or "when" of the data and is used to slice,
group, or filter data.

types.name: AnalyticsDimensionData
types.description:
Represents the specific values associated with a dimension in the context of analytics metrics.
This type is used to provide detailed information about the dimension's
specific data points, such as the value or identifier for each dimension instance.

types.name: AnalyticsMetric
types.description:
A metric is a quantitative value that measures performance or activity,
often derived from data to track goals or outcomes. It is a summarized
or calculated value used to assess trends or comparisons.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricCalculationType
types.description:
Defines the mathematical operation used to calculate a metric's value from
raw data. This enum describes how individual data points are aggregated
to produce the final metric value displayed in reports.

enumValues.name: SUM
enumValues.description: Adds all values in the dataset for the specified metric.

enumValues.name: AVERAGE
enumValues.description: Calculates the arithmetic mean of all values in the dataset.

enumValues.name: COUNT
enumValues.description: Returns the number of records or occurrences that match specific criteria.

enumValues.name: RATE
enumValues.description:
Computes the rate of a specific event or occurrence to the total
number of records or occurrences in the dataset.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricData
types.description:
Represents the data for a specific metric in the context of analytics metrics.
This interface is used to define the common structure for all metric data types,
allowing for polymorphic results.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricInsight
types.description:
Insight: An insight is a derived understanding or conclusion drawn from
data analysis, often providing actionable recommendations or highlighting
significant patterns or trends.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsBooleanFilterInput
types.description:
Allows filtering analytics data by matching a dimension against a specific boolean value.
The filter specifies a dimension ID and a boolean value (true or false) for that dimension.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the dimension to filter on.

inputFields.name: value
inputFields.description:
The boolean value to match against. Only data points where the dimension exactly
equals this value will be included in the results.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsFieldFilterInput
types.description:
Provides a way to specify different types of dimension filters for analytics metrics queries.
This input type functions as a "discriminated union" pattern, working around GraphQL's
limitation that doesn't allow union types for inputs.


Only one filter type should be specified per field filter. If multiple field values are provided,
an error will be raised and the operation will fail.

inputFields.name: stringFilter
inputFields.description:
A filter for exact string matching on dimension values.
Use this when you need to filter dimensions that contain string values.
each value in the array will result in a logical OR operation.

inputFields.name: booleanFilter
inputFields.description: A filter for matching dimension values against boolean values.

inputFields.name: idFilter
inputFields.description:
A filter for matching dimension values against a list of IDs.
Use this when you need to filter dimensions that contain ID values or
when you want to match a dimension against multiple possible values.

inputFields.name: radiusFilter
inputFields.description:
A filter for geographic radius search based on latitude and longitude.
Use this when you need to filter data within a specific geographic radius
around a given point.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsFilterInput
types.description:
Represents the filter criteria for querying analytics metrics, allowing
filters for specific dimensions. The dateRange filter and all fieldFilters will
be combined with a logical AND operation. However, within individual fieldFilters,
some expressions (such as ID lists in idFilter) operate as OR conditions, allowing for
selection of multiple values for a single dimension.

inputFields.name: fieldFilters
inputFields.description:
Optional list of dimension-specific filters to further refine the dataset.
Each field filter targets a specific dimension (like country, campaign, job category)

Multiple field filters are combined with logical AND operations, meaning data must
satisfy all provided filters to be included in the results.

For custom SQL parameters, use stringFilter with operation: CUSTOM where:
- id = parameter name (e.g., "partitionMonth")
- value = parameter value (e.g., "2023-12")

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsIdFilterInput
types.description:
Allows filtering analytics data by matching a dimension against a list of ID values.
The filter specifies a dimension ID and a list of acceptable values for that dimension.
Data points where the dimension matches ANY of the provided idValues will be included
in the results, effectively implementing a logical OR operation across the values.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the dimension to filter on.

inputFields.name: idValues
inputFields.description:
A list of values to filter on. If provided, only data points where the dimension matches
ANY of these values will be included in the results.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsRadiusFilterInput
types.description:
Allows filtering analytics data by geographic location within a specified radius.
This filter calculates a bounding box around the given latitude and longitude
and filters data that falls within the specified radius distance.

inputFields.name: latitude
inputFields.description: The latitude coordinate for the center point of the radius search.

inputFields.name: longitude
inputFields.description: The longitude coordinate for the center point of the radius search.

inputFields.name: radius
inputFields.description:
The radius distance for the search in miles.
This value will be automatically converted to kilometers for internal calculations.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsSortDirection
types.description: Sort directions supported by analytics metrics.

enumValues.name: ASCENDING
enumValues.description: Use ASCENDING for smallest-to-largest or A-Z ordering.

enumValues.name: DESCENDING
enumValues.description: Use DESCENDING for largest-to-smallest or Z-A ordering.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsSortInput
types.description:
Defines the sorting criteria for analytics metrics results.
This input type allows API consumers to specify a field to sort by and the direction
of the sort. The field can be either a dimension ID or a metric ID, providing
flexibility in how results are ordered.

inputFields.name: fieldId
inputFields.description:
The ID of the dimension or metric field to sort by. This should match the ID
of a dimension or metric defined in the schema.


When sorting by dimensions, results will be ordered alphabetically or numerically
based on the dimension values. When sorting by metrics, results will be ordered
based on the metric values.

inputFields.name: direction
inputFields.description:
The direction to sort the results.
Use ASCENDING for smallest-to-largest or A-Z ordering.
Use DESCENDING for largest-to-smallest or Z-A ordering.

types.name: AnalyticsMetricsStringFilterInput
types.description:
Allows filtering analytics data by matching a dimension against a specific string value.
The filter specifies a dimension ID and a string value for that dimension.
Data points where the dimension exactly matches the provided value will be included
in the results, implementing an equality comparison for string values.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: The ID of the dimension to filter on.

inputFields.name: operation
inputFields.description:
What logical operation to use when evaluating the
value.

inputFields.name: value
inputFields.description:
The string value to match against. Only data points where the dimension exactly
equals this string value will be included in the results.

types.name: AssetSchedule
types.description:
Cron scheduling configuration for an asset.

This configuration defines when and how an asset should be automatically triggered:
- enabled: Whether the schedule is active (when false, no Quartz jobs are created)
- cronExpressions: List of cron expressions defining trigger times
- schedulingWindow: Optional time window configuration for parameter calculation

The scheduling window is persisted with the asset and used during task execution,
not passed to the Quartz scheduler.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Whether the cron scheduling is enabled for this asset

fields.name: cronExpressions
fields.description: List of cron expressions that define when the asset should be triggered

fields.name: schedulingWindow
fields.description: Optional scheduling window configuration for calculating time-based parameters

types.name: AssetScheduleInput
types.description:
Input for configuring cron scheduling on an asset.

When enabled is true, the asset will be automatically triggered according to the
specified cron expressions. The scheduling window is used for time-based parameter
calculation during task execution.

Requirements:
- schedulingWindow is required when schedule is provided (both duration and offset must be specified)
- cronExpressions are required when enabled is true

inputFields.name: enabled
inputFields.description: Whether the cron scheduling should be enabled for this asset (defaults to false for safety)

inputFields.name: cronExpressions
inputFields.description: List of cron expressions that define when the asset should be triggered (required when enabled is true)

inputFields.name: schedulingWindow
inputFields.description: Scheduling window configuration for calculating time-based parameters (required when schedule is provided)

fields.name: initialize
fields.description:
Stages an application version to be published to Indeed. Application versions with file attachments will have presigned S3 URLs
generated, to which partners are expected to upload application file contents prior to submitting the application version
for processing.

The application version will not be published to Indeed until it is submitted. After staging, the application version
must be submitted within 5 minutes.

Initialization attempts for applications that have already been deleted will be rejected.

fields.name: submit
fields.description:
Submits an application version to be published to Indeed. Publishing of application versions is asynchronous, but will be processed
in the order in which they are submitted.

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Permanently deletes an application and all of its versions from Indeed. This is a terminal operation for the application specified,
and no further updates may be made to this application after deletion.

types.name: Availability
types.description:
Availability is an entity that stores the format and rules for generating available time slots,
including the scope (interview vs general), time slot details, and associated calendar information.

It serves as the foundation for querying available time periods for scheduling events.

fields.description: Availability IRI

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Specifies the scope level at which availability is defined at.

fields.name: timeSlotsConnection
fields.description: The time slots that are available based on the details and input provided.

fields.description: Type specific availability details.

types.description: Rule that defines a specific availability period of time.

fields.description: Globally unique rule id.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Rule identifier that is unique within the calendar, which is ASCII-only String of up to 64 characters.

fields.name: startTime
fields.description:
Start time of the rule period.

Resolution is 1 minute.

fields.name: endTime
fields.description:
End time of the rule period.

Value is greater than [startTime]. Resolution is 1 minute.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description:
The String that uniquely identifies the available period within an calendar.
The first request made for an Id will create an available period for the account and subsequent requests will update its details.

Usually this will be an internal ID for the available period, encoded as an ASCII-only String of up to 64 characters.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description:
Start time of the rule period.

Resolution is 1 minute. Any sub-minute portion of the value is dropped.

inputFields.name: endTime
inputFields.description:
End time of the rule period.

Value must be greater than [startTime] and less than 201 days from now.
Resolution is 1 minute. Any sub-minute portion of the value is dropped.

inputFields.name: maxWeight
inputFields.description:
maxWeight is ONE measure of the 'capacity' of this period. The weight for a period is the sum of all weights of appointments occurring during that time range.

Appointments can be booked for this period only while the period weight (including the new appointment) is less than or equal to the maxWeight.

In most cases, this value should be thought of as the number of humans conducting this interview. For 1:1 cases, this value should be 1.0 since there is only one human. For back-to-back cases where there could be multiple humans conducting appointments concurrently, this value could be > 1.0.

This value is NOT meant to be the same as an RSVP Cap. Please reach out to the S&A team if you have any questions.

maxWeight must be greater than 0.0. This value will only be used for Include Periods and should not be set on Exclude Periods.

types.name: AvailabilityScope
types.description: Specifies the scope level at which availability is defined at.

fields.name: week
fields.description: Weekly repeating rules.

fields.name: periods
fields.description:
Rules that specify specific time periods.

The periods are not empty. The periods may overlap or may be consecutive.

args.name: startTime
args.description: Start time of the periods to return or null to return all periods.

args.name: endTime
args.description:
End time of the periods to return or null for no limit.

Value must be greater than or equal to [startTime].

args.name: includeOverlapping
args.description:
True to include periods that overlap [startTime] or [endTime].

If true, return available periods whose start time is < [endTime] and
end time is > [startTime]. In other words, return periods where any part
of the periods overlaps the requested time range.

If false, return available periods whose start time is >= [startTime] and
end time is < [endTime]. In other words, return periods that are completely
contained within the requested time range.

args.name: first
args.description:
Maximum number of edges to return.

Value must be greater than zero. Default is determined by the server.

args.name: after
args.description: Retrieve edges after this cursor.

types.name: AvailabilitySlot
types.description: Period of time on a calendar that is available for scheduling an event.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Globally unique period id.

fields.name: startTime
fields.description:
Start time of the period.

Resolution is 1 minute.

fields.name: endTime
fields.description:
End time of the period.

Value is greater than [startTime]. Resolution is 1 minute.

fields.name: capacity
fields.description:
Number of events scheduled during this time period.

The events may be partially overlapping this period, so may be included in the
count for surrounding availability periods.

fields.name: count
fields.description:
Number of events currently scheduled during the time period.

The events may be partially overlapping this period, so may be included in the
count for surrounding availability periods.

enumValues.name: PERIODS
enumValues.description: Generate contiguous available periods that satisfy startInterval and are at least requiredDuration in length.

enumValues.name: AVAILABILITY_PERIODS
enumValues.description:
Generate slots that match the calendar availability settings. This will return time slots matching defined
availability periods and rules without any trimming or merging. There are several important qualities of this output
format:
1. Slots are not trimmed to the start and end times, and may extend past them.
2. Slots are not combined if overlapping or adjacent, so there may be overlapping slots.
3. Slots that would have any overlap with an exclude period are not returned.
4. Slots overlapping existing calendar events where the total weight + appointmentWeight > maxWeight are not returned.
5. Slots are only returned if their duration is equal to or greater than the requiredDuration argument.

enumValues.name: CONSISTENT_SLOTS
enumValues.description:
Generate available non-overlapping slots that satisfy requiredDuration and startInterval that will
not shift around due to changes in the availabilityWindow. (e.g. 10:00-12:00 availability; 1hr duration; 30m start
interval: slots returned would be 10:00-11:00 and 11:00-12:00 always. If the slot logic were not consistent and the
availabilityWindow start time was between 10:01 and 10:30, then only a single 10:30-11:30 slot would be returned)

enumValues.name: OVERLAPPING_SLOTS
enumValues.description: Generate all available slots that satisfy requiredDuration and startInterval even if the slots overlap eachother.

types.name: AvailabilitySlotsConnectionInput
types.description: Input to request availability slot connections for a given calendar configuration.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description:
Date/time to start listing availability from.

Value must be less than 201 days from now.

The default value will be `now()`

inputFields.name: endTime
inputFields.description:
Date/time to stop listing availability at.

Value must be at least 1 minute after the [startTime], less than 35 days from [startTime], and less than 201 days from now.

The default value will be 1 minute less than 35 days from [startTime].

inputFields.name: requiredDuration
inputFields.description:
Length of the returned availability periods.

Minimum value is 1 minute. Only hours and minutes are allowed.

inputFields.name: startInterval
inputFields.description:
Time intervals that returned periods will start on.

The default start interval depends on `outputFormat`.

inputFields.name: timeZone
inputFields.description:
Timezone Offset for requested availability

This should only be necessary if the timezone of the request is on a non-hour offset.
It will allow the [startInterval] to properly begin at the top of an hour in those timezones.

This value, if provided, will override the [startTime] offset.

inputFields.name: outputFormat
inputFields.description:
Controls the distribution of the returned slots. See [AvailabilitySlotFormat] for details.

Defaults to CONSISTENT_SLOTS.

inputFields.name: appointmentWeight
inputFields.description:
Appointment weight indicates how much a new appointment fills up a time slot. If the sum of appointment weights (including the new appointment)
is greater than the max weight for the availability slot, then the availability slot is unavailable. Value must be greater than or equal 0.
Defaults to 1.0.

fields.name: addEmployerJobs
fields.description:
Adds employer jobs to an existing billing identifier.

This mutation associates new employer jobs with the specified billing identifier.
- Jobs already associated with the billing identifier will be ignored.
- The operation only affects the specified jobs; existing associations remain unchanged
- If empty or null list provided, no jobs will be added

@returns The billing identifier and lists of added jobs

fields.name: removeEmployerJobs
fields.description:
Removes employer jobs from an existing billing identifier.

This mutation disassociates the specified employer jobs from the billing identifier.
- Jobs not currently associated with the billing identifier will be ignored.
- The operation only affects the specified jobs; other associations remain unchanged.
- If empty or null list provided, no jobs will be removed.

@returns The updated billing identifier and lists of removed jobs

types.name: BrsOptimizationType
types.description:
The type of campaign optimization

Campaign optimization in BRS happens through the [Budget Optimization](https://wiki.indeed.com/display/Enterprise/Budget+-+Optimization+Firebolt+Endpoint)
service where you can find more information about how the optimization parameters are used

enumValues.name: BALANCE
enumValues.description:
Balances the ratio of actual to target outcomes across jobs (i.e., if each job has a different minimum outcome
target – one job needs 15 apply starts and another needs 20 apply starts –then each job should be expected to
get the same fraction of the way to (or past) their target within the budget constraint)

enumValues.name: COVERAGE
enumValues.description:
If the campaign is infeasible under the maximum_budget constraint, results will be returned to meet job-level
constraints of as many jobs possible (regardless of the order they were input)

enumValues.name: DIMINISH
enumValues.description: Used in achieving diminishing returns at the job level. BRS is currently using a diminish exponent value of -0.5

enumValues.name: INFLECTION
enumValues.description: Bases job-level budget on points of inflection in yield curves

enumValues.name: PRIORITIZE
enumValues.description:
If the campaign is infeasible under the maximum_budget constraint, results will be returned to meet job-level
constraints of as many jobs as possible in the order they were input

enumValues.name: VOLUME
enumValues.description:
If the campaign is infeasible under the maximum_budget constraint, results will be returned that describe the
budget needed in order to meet job-level constraints of all jobs

fields.name: id
fields.description: Globally unique calendar id.

fields.name: availabilitySettings
fields.description:
Settings that define when the calendar is available to schedule events.

Availability settings can not absolutely prevent events that do not match the rules
from being scheduled on the calendar. They are rules that are applied during scheduling
unless specifically overridden.

fields.name: configurations
fields.description: Specifies a list of configurations for a calendar that define when the calendar is available to schedule events.

fields.name: available
fields.description:
Time periods that the calendar is available for scheduling, subject to the
[availabilityRules] and events that are scheduled on the calendar.

The time periods do not overlap and are not empty.

The periods may be consecutive. For example:
period1=2021-01-01T10:00-11:00Z, period2=2021-01-01T11:00-12:00Z

args.name: startTime
args.description:
Date/time to start listing availability from.

Value must be less than 201 days from now.

The default value will be `now()`

args.name: endTime
args.description:
Date/time to stop listing availability at.

Value must be at least 1 minute after the [startTime], less than 35 days from [startTime], and less than 201 days from now.

The default value will be 1 minute less than 35 days from [startTime].

args.name: requiredDuration
args.description:
Length of the returned availability periods.

Minimum value is 1 minute. Only hours and minutes are allowed.

args.name: startInterval
args.description:
Time intervals that returned periods will start on.

The default start interval depends on `outputFormat`.

args.name: timeZone
args.description:
Timezone Offset for requested availability

This should only be necessary if the timezone of the request is on a non-hour offset.
It will allow the [startInterval] to properly begin at the top of an hour in those timezones.

This value, if provided, will override the [startTime] offset.

args.name: first
args.description:
Maximum number of edges to return.

Value must be greater than zero. Default is determined by the server.

args.name: after
args.description: Retrieve edges after this cursor.

args.name: outputFormat
args.description:
Controls the distribution of the returned slots. See [AvailabilitySlotFormat] for details.

Defaults to CONSISTENT_SLOTS.

args.name: appointmentWeight
args.description:
Appointment weight indicates how much a new appointment fills up a time slot. If the sum of appointment weights (including the new appointment)
is greater than the max weight for the availability slot, then the availability slot is unavailable.

Value must be greater than or equal 0.

Defaults to 1.0.

types.name: CalendarAvailabilityGroupInput
types.description: Group of calendars to combine availability.

inputFields.name: calendars
inputFields.description:
Calendars in this group. Must not be empty. Duplicates are ignored.

Calendars (i.e. the calendar associated with the calendar configuration) in this list that are included
in periods from a parent group will be ignored. In other words, returned periods will not include the same
calendar multiple times.

inputFields.name: minimumCalendars
inputFields.description:
Minimum number of calendars from this group that must be available in a time period.

Minimum value is 0. A value greater than or equal to the length of the calendars field means that
all calendars must be available. A value of 0 will include all periods from the parent group, if any.

types.name: CalendarAvailabilityIdInput
types.description: Identify the calendar configuration to calculate availability from.

inputFields.name: calendarId
inputFields.description:
ID of the calendar to query availability from. Exactly one of accountKey or calendarId is required.

This can be a calendar id, a calendar configuration id, or the value "CURRENT_USER"
to use the calendar associated with the currently logged in user.

inputFields.name: accountKey
inputFields.description: ID of the Indeed account to query availability. Exactly one of accountKey or calendarId is required.

inputFields.name: configurationKey
inputFields.description:
Calendar configuration key to query availability from.

The key of a calendar configuration on the calendar referenced by the calendarId or accountKey field.
If not provided, the default configuration for the referenced calendar is used.
If the calendarId is a calendar configuration id and this field is provided, the
availability will be taken from the configuration with this key on the same calendar
associated with the configuration referenced by calendarId.

enumValues.description: Exclude all calendar events from the availability calculation.

fields.description: Rule identifier that is unique within the calendar configuration, which is ASCII-only String of up to 64 characters.

fields.description:
Start time of the rule period.

Resolution is 1 minute.

fields.name: endTime
fields.description:
End time of the rule period.

Value is greater than [startTime]. Resolution is 1 minute.

fields.name: maxWeight
fields.description:
maxWeight is ONE measure of the 'capacity' of this period. The weight for a period is the sum of all weights of appointments occurring during that time range.

Appointments can be booked for this period only while the period weight (including the new appointment) is less than or equal to the maxWeight.

In most cases, this value should be thought of as the number of humans conducting this interview. For 1:1 cases, this value should be 1.0 since there is only one human. For back-to-back cases where there could be multiple humans conducting appointments concurrently, this value could be > 1.0.

This value is NOT meant to be the same as an RSVP Cap. Please reach out to the S&A team if you have any questions.

maxWeight must be greater than 0.0. This value will only be used for Include Periods and should not be set on Exclude Periods.

fields.name: prorationBehavior
fields.description:
Defines the proration behavior for budget creates & updates during recurring periods.
Its values are String representation of 'CampaignBudgetProrationBehavior' enum.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations if unifiedProrationOptIn is true
- Cannot be used with Lifetime or AvgDaily recurring units
- Defaults to START_NOW_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets if not specified

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

fields.name: lastMonthProrationBehavior
fields.description:
Defines the budget behavior for the campaign's final month.
Its values are String representation of 'CampaignBudgetLastMonthProrationBehavior' enum.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- The value is only considered when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled (true)
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled
- When a campaign's first and last month are the same, prorationBehavior setting takes precedence
- Cannot be used with Lifetime or AvgDaily recurring units
- Works in conjunction with the general prorationBehavior setting
- Controls budget allocation specifically for the campaign's final month
- If not specified, defaults to LAST_MONTH_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

fields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during budget change.
It's values are String representation of 'CampaignProrationPeriodResetSubRange' enum.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for prorated budget calculation unless explicitly modified
- Required budget change to new value during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates.
Defaults to FIRST_MONTH_ONLY, unless explicitly set during creation or updates during an budget change.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

fields.name: resetProrationOnReactivation
fields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during campaign reactivation.
It's values are String representation of 'CampaignProrationPeriodResetSubRange' enum.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for recalculation unless explicitly modified
- Requires status change to ACTIVE during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future prorated budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates.
Defaults to NEVER, unless explicitly set during creation or modified during an update.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

types.name: CampaignDeliveryObjectiveLegacyPreset
types.description:
Defines the preset delivery objective configuration which corresponds to a legacy objective type used by enterprise clients.
This is regarded as the source-of-truth of objectives for such clients.

This enum is non-exhaustive and new values might be added.

Legacy objectives are implemented through delivery objectives as follows -

| Legacy Preset  | Objective      | Supported Configuration                   |
|----------------|----------------|-------------------------------------------|
| BALANCE        | CLICK          | CampaignBalancingStrategyBalancedOutcomes |
| BUDGET         | CLICK          | CampaignBalancingStrategyNoBalance        |
| INTERVIEW      | INTERVIEW_RSVP | CampaignBalancingStrategyCustomTarget     |
| QUICK          | CLICK          | CampaignPacingStrategyAccelerated         |
| TARGET_APPLIES | APPLY          | CampaignBalancingStrategyCustomTarget     |
| TCPA           | APPLY          | CampaignCostControlCostCap                |
| UNSPECIFIED    | CLICK          | No configuration                          |

enumValues.name: UNSPECIFIED
enumValues.description:
"
The UNSPECIFIED preset signifies that the Campaign has no legacy objective type associated with it.
Note that it is not equivalent to a missing `legacyPreset` field,
which means that an existing delivery objective for the Campaign cannot be defined
in terms of a legacy preset which is interpretable by enterprise clients.

default: 0

fields.name: pageSize
fields.description:
Page size considered while prefetching cursors.
Use this as 'first' or 'last' argument to fetch pages from prefetched cursors.

fields.name: endCursors
fields.description:
When paginating forwards, returns the cursors of the next few pages of fixed size.
This is only present in case of forward pagination.
This will be an empty list in case of backward pagination.
The first element is the cursor to fetch the next page, subsequent elements are cursors for pages after that.
The first element is the same as endCursor of this current page.

fields.name: startCursors
fields.description:
When paginating backward, returns the cursors of the previous few pages of fixed size.
This is only present in case of backward pagination.
This will be an empty list in case of forward pagination.
The last element is the cursor to fetch the previous page, prior elements are cursors for pages before that.
The last element is the same as startCursor of this current page.

types.name: CampaignSchedule
types.description:
A value object that defines the campaign schedule to
specify the start and end datetime of the campaign.

fields.name: startDateTime
fields.description:
When the campaign should become active. This field affects
the budget by the prorationBehavior field.
Optional, campaign will start spending immediately if input is not provided.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

fields.name: endDateTime
fields.description:
When the campaign should become inactive. This field affects
the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

fields.name: targetEndDateTime
fields.description:
When the campaign should optimize for the desired outcome.
Campaign is allowed to continue to spend past this date.
This field affects the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none. Cannot be set at the same time when endDateTime is also set.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

fields.name: extEndDateTime
fields.description:
This captures the user specified end date for the campaign
Can be none if the campaign is open ended. This is only supported for hosted monthly and daily campaigns.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

types.name: CampaignScheduleUsCentralDate
types.description:
A value object that defines the campaign schedule to
specify the start and end date of the campaign.

Date and time in this object is always converted to US/Central
time and truncated to the date granularity.

fields.name: startDate
fields.description:
When the campaign should become active. This field affects
the budget by the prorationBehavior field.
Optional, campaign is paused if it has no startDate.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.

fields.name: endDate
fields.description:
When the campaign should become inactive. This field affects
the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.

fields.name: targetEndDate
fields.description:
When the campaign should optimize for the desired outcome.
Campaign is allowed to continue to spend past this date.
This field affects the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none. Cannot be set at the same time when endDateTime is also set.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.

NOTE: This input field is still unused and ignored.

If more than one entity of the same type is provided, those will be considered ORed.
If more than one entity type is provided, those will be considered ANDed.
For example, if we receive a entry of type candidate submission with values x and y, and another entry for related feedback with value z,
it would return feedback linked to submission x related to feedback z, along with submission y related to feedback z.

Connection to a list of CandidateSubmissionGroup

The input argument can be used to filter the list of groups returned.  If input is set to a non-null value, the first and
after arguments will be ignored.  If input is not set, or is set to null, any groups that contain the CandidateSubmission
will be returned.

to which the requesting user has not been granted access, the connection will include a null element and a FORBIDDEN error
will be returned for each such group.

types.name: CirrusTriggerSubscriptionMutations
types.description: Cirrus Trigger Subscription Mutations

fields.name: enable
fields.description:
Enable subscriptions for the given job request's linked employer jobs. Partial successes are allowed
and any errors will be returned in the payload.

- If the employer job does not have a subscription, a new subscription will be created.
- If the employer job already has a subscription but is not enabled or does not have the correct
workflow type (from the input), the subscription will be updated.
- If the employer job already has a subscription and is already enabled and has the correct workflow type,
no update will be made.
- If there is an error updating an employer job, the job is omitted from the response data

fields.name: disable
fields.description:
Disable subscriptions for the given job request's linked employer jobs. Partial successes are allowed
and any errors will be returned in the payload.

- If the employer job has an enabled subscription, the subscription will be updated to disabled
- If the employer job has a disabled subscription, no update will be made
- If there is an error updating an employer job, the job is omitted from the response data

inputFields.description:
Defines the recurring duration of the budget.
For example if it’s monthly then the total budget is refreshed monthly by the limit amount.
Must be defined.

inputFields.name: prorationBehavior
inputFields.description:
Defines the proration behavior for budget creates & updates during recurring periods.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations if unifiedProrationOptIn is true
- Defaults to START_NOW_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets if not specified

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

inputFields.name: lastMonthProrationBehavior
inputFields.description:
Defines the behavior for the last month of the recurring duration.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- The value is only considered when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled (true)
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled
- When a campaign's first and last month are the same, prorationBehavior setting takes precedence
- Works in conjunction with the general prorationBehavior setting
- Controls budget allocation specifically for the campaign's final month
- If not specified, defaults to LAST_MONTH_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

inputFields.name: limit

types.name: CreateCampaignProrationOptionsInput
types.description: Defines settings that control budget proration behavior during campaign lifecycle.

inputFields.name: resetProrationOnBudgetChange
inputFields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during budget changes.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for prorated budget calculation unless explicitly modified
- Required budget change to new value during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates. Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
Defaults to FIRST_MONTH_ONLY, unless explicitly set during creation.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

inputFields.name: resetProrationOnReactivation
inputFields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during campaign reactivation.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for recalculation unless explicitly modified
- Requires status change to ACTIVE during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future prorated budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates. Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
Defaults to NEVER, unless explicitly set during creation.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

types.name: CreateCampaignScheduleInput
types.description: The schedule input for creating a Campaign.

inputFields.name: startDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become active. This field affects
the budget by the prorationBehavior field.
Optional, campaign is paused if it has no startDate.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

inputFields.name: endDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become inactive. This field affects
the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

Setting both the endDateTime and targetEndDateTime is unsupported and may result in unspecified behavior.
In addition, targetEndDateTime cannot be used with MONTHLY recurring budget.

inputFields.name: targetEndDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should optimize for the desired outcome.
Campaign is allowed to continue to spend past this date.
This field affects the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none. Cannot be set at the same time when endDateTime is also set.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.

Setting both the endDateTime and targetEndDateTime is unsupported and may result in unspecified behavior.
In addition, targetEndDateTime cannot be used with MONTHLY recurring budget.

inputFields.name: extEndDateTime
inputFields.description:
This field captures the user-specified end date for the campaign, stored as an RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset.
Can be null if the campaign is open ended. This field preserves the original end date specified by the user.

Important restrictions:
- Cannot be used in conjunction with endDateTime or targetEndDateTime
- Only supported for hosted monthly and daily campaigns
- Requires isHosted field to be set to true or false

inputFields.name: startUsCentralDate
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become active. This field affects
the budget by the prorationBehavior field.
Optional, campaign is paused if it has no startDate.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.
inputFields.deprecationReason: Should always use UTC timezone for consistency so use startDateTime.

inputFields.name: endUsCentralDate
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become inactive. This field affects
the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.
inputFields.deprecationReason: Should always use UTC timezone for consistency so use endDateTime.

inputFields.name: targetEndUsCentralDate
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should optimize for the desired outcome.
Campaign is allowed to continue to spend past this date.
This field affects the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none. Cannot be set at the same time when endDateTime is also set.

An RFC-3339 encoded date string.
Time is always converted to US/Central time and truncated to the
date granularity.
inputFields.deprecationReason: Should always use UTC timezone for consistency so use targetEndDateTime.

inputFields.description:

inputFields.description:
A list of AdGroups related to the campaign. They provide a way to create multi-objective

inputFields.name: upid
inputFields.description:
The UX-Product identifier allows the platform to select different handlers
for different product or product versions.
For now this is only visible to trusted internal systems.

inputFields.name: experimental
inputFields.description:
A namespace for experimental campaign properties.
Note: Please plan for migration in the future if you plan to use these properties.

inputFields.name: idempotencyKey
inputFields.description:
Allow retrying requests without performing the same operation twice.

Client must supply a unique value generated by the client. We suggest
using V4 UUIDs, or another random string with enough entropy.

Keys guarantee up to 24 hours of idempotency. After that same key can be
used again.

Note: we haven't really talked about the guarantee & implementation around
idempotency so please consider the key and the doc a placeholder.

inputFields.name: extRefId

Allows you to reference a campaign with an external system id.
If the extRefId already exists for an Employer then campaign creation fails.

- example: `2345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef`

Enables checks and validations specific to single job campaigns managed by the hosted jobs platform.
If not specified, defaults to false. Cannot be set to true if upid is set, as upid and isHosted=true are mutually exclusive.

The only exception to this rule is jobs - invalid/missing jobs will be excluded from the draft, but
valid jobs will still be added to the draft.

For example, a missing address for an in-person interview method will result in a null "method" section of the
draft, which must be populated by update before the event can be published.

types.name: CreateVirtualInterviewEventInput
types.description: Input object for the `createVirtualInterviewEvent` mutation.

inputFields.name: interviewers
inputFields.description:
One or more interviewer email addresses.

**Notes:**

* When you schedule an event, the API automatically adds you as an interviewer to the event.
* You can add an interviewee and interviewers to an event after you schedule it.

**Validation error:** If the total number of interviewers exceeds 49, a validation error occurs.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description: Interview start time, in [RFC3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) format with a time zone offset.

inputFields.name: endTime
inputFields.description:
Interview end time, in [RFC3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) format with a time zone offset.

**Validation error:** If the interview duration is greater than 24 hours, a validation error occurs. That is, if the `endTime` value minus `startTime` value is greater than 24 hours.

inputFields.name: timezone
inputFields.description: Time zone for the interview, in [IANA Time Zone Database](https://www.iana.org/time-zones) format. Displays the time zone in the event for both the interviewee and interviewers. The time zone value is separate from the `startTime` and `endTime` offset.

inputFields.name: title
inputFields.description: Title of the interview, which is usually the calendar event title.

inputFields.name: interviewee
inputFields.description:
Name and email of the interviewee.

If you don’t have the name of the interviewee, omit this field.

To add the interviewee to the interview event later, use the `updateVirtualInterviewEvent` mutation.

inputFields.name: requestMetadata
inputFields.description:
Information about the request:

* Partner application, which is usually an application tracking system (ATS), from which the request was sent.
* Employer name, if available.

inputFields.name: languageCode
inputFields.description:
Language code, in lowercase.

If you provide `countryCode`, `languageCode` is required.

**Validation error:** If you provide `countryCode` without `languageCode`, a validation error occurs.

If you omit both `languageCode` and `countryCode`, the default `languageCode` value is `en` and the default `countryCode` value is `US`.

If you include `languageCode` and omit `countryCode`, `languageCode` is the value you specify and `countryCode` is null.

inputFields.name: countryCode
inputFields.description:
Country code, in uppercase.

If you provide `countryCode`, `languageCode` is required.

**Validation error:** If you provide `countryCode` without `languageCode`, a validation error occurs.

If you omit both `languageCode` and `countryCode`, the default `languageCode` value is `en` and the default `countryCode` value is `US`.

If you include `languageCode` and omit `countryCode`, `languageCode` is the value you specify and `countryCode` is null.

inputFields.description:
This screener question type requires either the dd/MM/yyyy format or a locale-specific format that meets Unicode CLDR formatting.

Indeed uses the `SimpleDateFormat`. You must format the month as MM. Using mm results in misconfiguration.

The format of `type=date` impacts how the application is passed to the ATS and how the minimum and maximum values are parses. The job seeker still enters the date based on their locale, not the specified format, and validation error messages are in their locale’s format. To prevent confusion, use yyyy instead of yy in the format.

types.description:
A dedicated scheduling format is an entity that defines how to schedule appointments by storing scheduling
preferences and referencing a single [calendarId] for availability.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Globally unique scheduling format id.

fields.name: displayName
fields.description: Plain text display name of the scheduling format.

fields.name: participantGroups
fields.description:
List of participant groups to reference availability and preferences when generating the scheduling slots.

At least 1 participant group with at least 1 required participant is required.

fields.name: startInterval
fields.description: Time intervals that returned scheduling slots will start on.

fields.name: outputFormat
fields.description: Controls the distribution of the returned slots.

fields.name: timeZone
fields.description:
Timezone Offset for requested availability

This should only be necessary if the timezone of the request is on a non-hour offset.
It will allow the [startInterval] to properly begin at the top of an hour in those timezones.

This value, if provided, will override the [startTime] offset for purposes of calculating [startInterval].

fields.name: schedulingSlotsConnection
fields.description:
Find the time periods that the calendar is available for scheduling, subject to the scheduling preferences
and the appointments that are scheduled on the calendar,

The time periods do not overlap and are not empty.

The periods may be consecutive. For example:e
period1=2021-01-01T10:00-11:00Z, period2=2021-01-01T11:00-12:00Z

types.description: For detailed info about screener question, please go to https://docs.indeed.com/dev/reference/screener-questions

inputFields.name: textarea
inputFields.description: A question that requires a long-form answer. Appears as a multi-line text entry field.

inputFields.name: text
inputFields.description:
A question that requires a short answer. Appears as a single-line text entry field.

For more information on the available formats for text questions, see the following examples and the [JSON questions parameters](https://docs.indeed.com/indeed-apply/screener-questions#json-questions-parameters). The formats are `integer`, `decimal`, and `numeric_text`.

inputFields.name: select
inputFields.description:
A question with multiple choice answers. Appears as a dropdown list that enables the applicant to select a single answer.

If you include from one to five answers, each answer appears with a radio button. If you include more than five answers, they appear in a dropdown list.

inputFields.name: multiselect
inputFields.description: A question that has multiple answers. Appears as a list of checkboxes that enables the applicant to select multiple answers.

inputFields.name: date
inputFields.description:
A question that has a date as an answer. Appears as a text field that accepts a date.

This screener question type requires either the dd/MM/yyyy format or a locale-specific format that meets Unicode CLDR formatting.

Indeed uses the `SimpleDateFormat`. You must format the month as MM. Using mm results in misconfiguration.

The format of `type=date` impacts how the application is passed to the ATS and how the minimum and maximum values are parses. The job seeker still enters the date based on their locale, not the specified format, and validation error messages are in their locale’s format. To prevent confusion, use yyyy instead of yy in the format.

inputFields.name: information
inputFields.description:
A text display that does not require a response. Appears as explanatory text or section headings.
For details, see [information](https://docs.indeed.com/indeed-apply/screener-questions#information).

inputFields.name: pageBreak
inputFields.description: Groups questions on a page. Questions defined between two pagebreak types appear on the same page. You can group up to 20 questions on a page. By default, Indeed shows three questions on a page on desktop and groups all questions on a page for mobile.

types.name: DeploymentMutations
types.description:
Namespace type containing all deployment-related mutations.
Provides organized access to deployment, policy, and service account operations.

fields.name: create
fields.description: Creates a new deployment with the provided configuration

fields.name: delete
fields.description: Deletes a deployment by its unique ID

fields.name: update
fields.description: Updates an existing deployment with the provided configuration

fields.name: addPolicies
fields.description: Adds one or more policies to an existing deployment in a single transaction

fields.name: updatePolicies
fields.description: Updates one or more policies within an existing deployment in a single transaction

fields.name: removePolicies
fields.description: Removes one or more policies from an existing deployment in a single transaction

fields.name: resync
fields.description:
Triggers resynchronization of all stale policies in a deployment.
By default, only policies where lastModifiedAt > lastSuccessfulSyncAt are resynced.
Use force=true to resync all policies regardless of their current sync status.

fields.name: resyncPolicy
fields.description:
Triggers resynchronization of specific policies within a deployment.
By default, only resyncs if policies are stale (lastModifiedAt > lastSuccessfulSyncAt).
Use force=true to resync regardless of current sync status.
If policyNames is null or empty, all policies in the deployment will be resynced.
Requires authorization - only the deployment owner can trigger policy resync.

fields.name: upsertServiceAccount
fields.description:
Creates or updates a service account registration for a deployment
Queues UPDATE message for async processing

fields.name: updateServiceAccountArchetype
fields.description:
Updates the archetype username and user groups of a service account registration
Queues UPDATE message for async processing

fields.name: removeServiceAccount
fields.description:
Removes the service account registration from a deployment
Queues DELETE message for async processing

fields.name: resyncServiceAccount
fields.description:
Triggers resynchronization of a service account registration
Queues UPDATE message to force reconciliation with SAM

fields.name: clientMetaState
fields.description:
Any client can persist data that is relevant to its specific client flow in this field so that client can look up values later on.
Those data are only persisted in the application draft and will not be delivered to employers.

The total number of key-value pairs in the list can not exceed 50.

The client will be responsible for populating and maintaining this field.
This includes, but may not be limited to:
When populating the field, ensuring they are not wiping away existing state unintentionally
When clearing/removing fields (or the object), ensuring they are not destroying state they are not responsible for.
Understanding how to properly decode the key/value pairs they are interested in.

Refer to the DraftManagementAdditionalProperty type to see the constraints and recommendations on this field.

fields.name: internalContext
fields.description:

Note: If non-authorized clients attempt to use this field the operation will fail.

Note: It will NOT be included in application delivered content.

The total number of key-value pairs in the list can not exceed 50.

The client will be responsible for populating and maintaining this field.
This includes, but may not be limited to:
When populating the field, ensuring they are not wiping away existing state unintentionally
When clearing/removing fields (or the object), ensuring they are not destroying state they are not responsible for.
Understanding how to properly decode the key/value pairs they are interested in.

Refer to the DraftManagementAdditionalProperty type to see the constraints and recommendations on this field.

fields.name: externalContext
fields.description:
External context fields that can store additional properties that is not present in the current draft schema. It acts a way
to provide data to be used by external systems.

Note: It will be included in application delivered content.

The total number of key-value pairs in the list can not exceed 50.

The client will be responsible for populating and maintaining this field.
This includes, but may not be limited to:
When populating the field, ensuring they are not wiping away existing state unintentionally
When clearing/removing fields (or the object), ensuring they are not destroying state they are not responsible for.
Understanding how to properly decode the key/value pairs they are interested in.

Refer to the DraftManagementAdditionalProperty type to see the constraints and recommendations on this field.

joinedInterviewerAccounts is a set of encrypted accountIds related to

This excludes interviewers who have only taken the action
INTERVIEWER_ARRIVED for hosted or in-person events.
Presence in this set does not guarantee that the
interviewer actually connected with the jobseeker.

fields.name: initialConnectionStartTime
fields.description:
an ISO 8601 date-time format with UTC timezone
(e.g. '2011-12-03T10:15:30Z') that represents when any
interviewer initially connected with the jobseeker.
Only present if an interviewer ever connected with the jobseeker.
For example, if an interviewer and jobseeker connect from
'2023-01-01T12:00:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:05:00Z' and again from
'2023-01-01T12:10:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:15:00Z', the
initialConnectionStartTime will be '2023-01-01T12:00:00Z'

fields.name: mostRecentConnectionStartTime
fields.description:
an ISO 8601 date-time format with UTC timezone
(e.g. '2011-12-03T10:15:30Z') that represents when any
interviewer most recently started a connection with the
Jobseeker.
Only present if a connection ever started.
For example, if an interviewer and jobseeker connect from
'2023-01-01T12:00:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:05:00Z' and again from
'2023-01-01T12:10:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:15:00Z', the
mostRecentConnectionStartTime would be will be
'2023-01-01T12:10:00Z'

fields.name: mostRecentConnectionEndTime
fields.description:
an ISO 8601 date-time format with UTC timezone
(e.g. '2011-12-03T10:15:30Z') that represents when any
interviewer most recently ended a connection with the jobseeker.
Only present if an connection ever ended.
For example, if an interviewer and jobseeker connect from
'2023-01-01T12:00:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:05:00Z' and again from
'2023-01-01T12:10:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:15:00Z', the
mostRecentConnectionEndTime would be will be
'2023-01-01T12:15:00Z'

fields.name: connectionDuration
fields.description:
ISO 8601 duration (e.g. 'PT17M20S'). Only present if at least one
connection start and one connection end signal have been added to
the summary (note that this is not a guarantee; it's possible for
the summary to have both start and end signals and for the connection
duration to be null). If there are multiple connections represented
by one ICR summary, the duration will aggregate these connection
times. For example, if an interviewer and jobseeker connect from
'2023-01-01T12:00:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:05:00Z' and again from
'2023-01-01T12:10:00Z' to '2023-01-01T12:15:00Z', the
connectionDuration will be 'PT10M'

fields.name: userGroupAssignments
fields.description:
A list of all user groups for which (1) the user is a member of the user group
and (2) the user group has permissions on the user's current employer.

Example:
**STATE**
Employer [E1] grant Jobs access to user group [UG1]
User [U1] has Member access on Employer [E1]

**OUTCOME**
[U1] userGroups will be empty

**STATE CHANGE**
[U1] is added to user group [UG1]

**OUTCOME**
UserGroups now returns [UG1]

**STATE CHANGE**
[U1] switches advertisers to unrelated Employer [E2]
[E2] does not grant access to any user groups

**OUTCOME**
[U1] userGroups will be empty

types.name: EmployerUserPermissions
types.description:
Represents a user's permissions on different resources

Consumers can directly query for the user's permissions on a specific resource by selecting the appropriate field.

Note: New permissions and verbs are added from time to time.
The field `EmployerUserPermissions.permissionStrings` is available for applications that need a future-proof means
to get the "complete" set of permissions for the user, even if new permissions/verbs are added.
However `permissionStrings` is not recommended for applications that need to check whether the user has certain specific permission(s).

fields.name: permissionStrings
fields.description:
Array that contains all permissions associated with the account.

This should be used when all the permissions the user has are needed, not when checking if the user has a specific permission

fields.name: name

fields.name: description
fields.description: A text description of what the permission set gives access to do

fields.name: permissions
fields.description: The specific permissions granted by the permission set

fields.name: editable
fields.description: Whether or not users are allowed to add or remove this permission set

fields.name: selectedByDefault
fields.description: Whether or not the permission set is selected by default when inviting a new user

fields.name: isAdmin
fields.description: Whether or not the permission set is an admin permission set. Note that there are multiple distinct permission sets considered admin permission sets (namely, at this time, Admin and Job Admin)

fields.name: limited
fields.description: Whether or not the permission set is a limited fine-grained permission set

types.name: EmployerVerificationOption
types.description:
Options which can be presented to a user for them to verify for elevated privileges.

The degree to which each option escalates a user's privileges depends on the option and
the confidence we have in it preventing fraud. That information is not represented here
as its business logic changes with experimentation and other criteria.

In all options, some set of information provided for verification is made available for
future moderation as well as for cross-referencing fraud case data. See individual option
descriptions for more information. This recorded information is subject to standard PII
handling and often has TTLs related to preserve PII privacy. Some of this information
is hashed for linking accounts and fraud-related indicators for future moderation.

enumValues.name: INBOUND_CALLING
enumValues.description:
Option by which an employer can call a phone number to speak with a moderator and present
information required for verification. The outcome of this option depends on moderator decisions,
information presented, and information available. Preserved information depends on what is noted
as part of the moderation process.

***Note*: This is a "manual" moderation option, meaning it has human time cost.**

enumValues.name: DOCUMENT_UPLOAD
enumValues.description:
Option which queries an employer for various pieces of information needed to make a verification
decision including documents that prove employer legitimacy. These documents are then scanned
and made available to moderators for asynchronous evaluation.

All provided information is made available to moderators.

***Note*: This is a "manual" moderation option, meaning it has human time cost.**

enumValues.name: ID_ME
enumValues.description:
US-only automated verification option through a vendor that verifies the legitimacy of
the person being verified via evaluation of government approved identification documents.

A minimum of the verified person information is made available to moderators.

enumValues.name: GSTIN
enumValues.description:
India-only automated verification option that allows verification using employer tax ID and
mobile phone registration. This information is used to verify government registration and that
the person requesting verification is associated with the company.

IDs and other information available from the government is made available to moderators.

enumValues.name: CORPORATE_EMAIL
enumValues.description:
Automated email verification option for users who signed up with a non-company-associated email.
Users can provide a company associated email and verify their ownership of it.

The verified email is made available to moderators.

enumValues.name: PAYMENT
enumValues.description:
Automated verification option that allows users to verify via a test charge to a payment option.

Payment reference information is preserved and can be cross-referenced with payments APIs.
No related PII is recorded to moderation systems.

enumValues.name: PERSONA
enumValues.description:
Internationally-available automated verification option through a vendor that verifies the legitimacy of
the person being verified via evaluation of government approved identification documents.

A minimum of the verified person information is made available to moderators.

types.name: EmployerVerificationPayload
types.description:
Payload for queries for employer verification data. Keyed by `id` (encrypted advertiserId aka advertiserNumber)
for caching purposes.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
Encrypted advertiserId / advertiserNumber, returned/keyed on for caching purposes. This should be queried
along with every other field in this payload or results will not be cached. See individual fields for cache
time suggestions to be set by clients.

fields.name: availableOptions
fields.description:
List of verification options available for this employer to use to complete verification.

The presence of options should not be used to indicate verification eligibility as these
are likely to be derived independently of eligibility in the future. See the future `verificationEligibility`
field to be added.

This field should be cached a maximum of 5 minutes currently, as that is the expected maximum duration of
asynchronous processes that might change these results.

fields.name: nudgedOptions
fields.description:
List of verification options that should be presented to the user with higher priority for any reason.
These are not guaranteed at this time to be in any sort of priority order and only indicate that
these particular options are a higher priority subset of `availableOptions`.

Cache time for this field should match `availableOptions` as the same limitations apply.

***Note*: `VerificationOption.ID_ME` should never be nudged due to legal concerns.**

fields.name: availabilities
fields.description:
List of verification availability statuses that indicate the high-level verification state
for this employer. These indicate if an employer should be directed to verify and what type
of verification flow they should be presented with.

Cache time for this field should match `availableOptions` as the same limitations apply.

Use this ID to expire the job posting.

Internal tracking ID from logrepo.

Note: Only one of 'sort' (single criteria) or 'sorts' (multiple criteria) can be provided.

enumValues.name: END_DATETIME_ASC
enumValues.description: Corresponds to CampaignSchedule.endDateTime

enumValues.name: END_DATETIME_DESC
enumValues.description: Corresponds to CampaignSchedule.endDateTime

enumValues.name: SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY_ASC
enumValues.description:
Sort by spending eligibility in ascending order.

Order: FULL_SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY -> USER_SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY -> FUNDED_PERIOD_ELIGIBILITY -> SCHEDULED_PERIOD_ELIGIBILITY -> PREMIUM_FEATURE_ELIGIBILITY

Maps to CampaignSpendingEligibilityEnum values.
Reference: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/_YuVEw

Note: Spending eligibility is only available for active campaigns. Non-active campaigns
are sorted to the end (for ASC) or beginning (for DESC) of the results.

When a campaign has multiple eligibility types, precedence is given according to the
presence of the specified eligibility in the sort order above.

enumValues.name: SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY_DESC
enumValues.description:
Sort by spending eligibility in descending order.

Order: PREMIUM_FEATURE_ELIGIBILITY -> SCHEDULED_PERIOD_ELIGIBILITY -> FUNDED_PERIOD_ELIGIBILITY -> USER_SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY -> FULL_SPENDING_ELIGIBILITY

Maps to CampaignSpendingEligibilityEnum values.
Reference: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/_YuVEw

Note: Spending eligibility is only available for active campaigns. Non-active campaigns
are sorted to the beginning (for DESC) or end (for ASC) of the results.

When a campaign has multiple eligibility types, precedence is given according to the
presence of the specified eligibility in the sort order above.

enumValues.name: STATUS_ASC
enumValues.description:
Sort by campaign status in ascending order.

Order: ACTIVE -> PAUSED -> ARCHIVED

Maps to CampaignStatus enum values.

enumValues.name: STATUS_DESC
enumValues.description:
Sort by campaign status in descending order.

Order: ARCHIVED -> PAUSED -> ACTIVE

Maps to CampaignStatus enum values.

types.description:
The input object used when requesting multiple interviews. Only one of the non-`clientFilterTypes` fields can be
provided per query. Note that, if the calling user has FGP enabled (ie the ACCESS_AS_GRANTED role) this endpoint will
only return the subset of interviews they have access to.

inputFields.name: byCandidateSubmission
inputFields.description: Get a list of Interviews for a given Candidate Submission UUID

inputFields.name: timeRange
inputFields.description:
Get a list of SCHEDULED Interviews for an advertiser with start times within the provided range (see the input
object for more details)

inputFields.name: allByTimeRange
inputFields.description:
Get a list of all Interviews for an advertiser within a time range. This includes all interviews *except*
invalidated interviews. For scheduled interviews, an interview is returned if and only if its start time falls
within the provided time range. For non-scheduled interviews with proposed times, an interview is returned if
*any* of its proposed times fall within the provided range. All non-scheduled availability based interviews are returned

inputFields.name: scheduledForAdvertiser
inputFields.description: Get all Interviews for an advertiser that have the status SCHEDULED (see the input object for more details)

inputFields.name: unscheduledForAdvertiser
inputFields.description: Get all Interviews for an advertiser that do NOT have the status SCHEDULED (see the input object for more details)

inputFields.name: allByStatus
inputFields.description: Get all interviews for an advertiser that are in one of the provided statuses (see the input object for more details)

inputFields.name: byInterviewAggregationReference
inputFields.description: Get a list of Interviews for a given aggregation reference

inputFields.name: clientFilters
inputFields.description:
Optional. A list of filters (not owned by IMP) to apply to the interviews returned by this endpoint. These
filters have "and" semantics - ie an interview will only be returned if it isn't filtered out by *any* of the
filters in the list. Note that these filters are applied *in addition to* any other filters specified in the query

inputFields.name: sortOptionInput
inputFields.description:
Optional. This variable contains sorting option for this query. Note that this input is currently not available for
byCandidateSubmission query.

inputFields.name: byCoordinationType
inputFields.description:
Optional. If not present, only managed interviews will be returned. This input field can be used in combination
with byCandidateSubmission, allByStatus, allUpcomingInterviews, allPastInterviews, or allPendingInterviews.
This field will be removed in the future because all surfaces eventually should handle both managed and
ad hoc interviews, but for now, this field is default to MANAGED_ONLY.

inputFields.name: allUpcomingInterviews
inputFields.description:
Get a list of upcoming Interviews. The returned interviews will be sorted by effective end time of the interview.
By default, this filter queries interviews with effective end time > now + 1 minute.

inputFields.name: allPastInterviews
inputFields.description:
Get a list of past Interviews. The returned interviews will be sorted by effective end time of the interview.
By default, this filter queries interviews with effective end time <= now.

inputFields.name: allPendingInterviews
inputFields.description: Get a list of pending Interviews. The returned interviews will be sorted by last modified time.
