types.name: FindEmployerJobsFilterInput
types.description:
Each filter expression should consist of a single-arity object that contains either the field name or compound operator
and its value. If multiple operators or fields are supplied they will implicitly form an "allOf" filter. Filters can
be nested to build more complex filters.

inputFields.name: not
inputFields.description: Negates the provided child filter.

inputFields.name: anyOf
inputFields.description: Includes an employer job if any of the provided filters match.

inputFields.name: allOf
inputFields.description: Only includes an employer job if all of the provided filters match.

inputFields.name: sourceId
inputFields.description: Filter on the sourceId field.

inputFields.name: title
inputFields.description: Filter on the title field

inputFields.name: location
inputFields.description: Filter on the location attributes

inputFields.name: referenceId
inputFields.description: Filter on the referenceId also known as the "refnum."

inputFields.name: externalRequisitionId
inputFields.description: Filter on the external job requisition identifier

inputFields.name: externalJobPostId
inputFields.description: Filter on the externalJobPostId.

inputFields.name: publishedDateTime
inputFields.description:
Filter on the date that the employer job was "published" with date in CDT. This is a best guess at when the job was
first created and not necessarily when it was first aggregated by Indeed.

inputFields.name: datePostedOnIndeed
inputFields.description:
Filter on the date that the employer job was originally published in CDT. This date represents the date time that
the job post was indexed by job seeker search and available on Indeed.com if the job was visible.

inputFields.name: createdOnIndeed
inputFields.description:
If true returns jobs that were originally created on Indeed. If false returns jobs that were originally created
externally (eg. via an ATS).

inputFields.name: postedOnIndeed
inputFields.description: DO NOT USE. IGNORED.

inputFields.name: legacyClaimed
inputFields.description:
If true, returns only jobs that were claimed via the legacy (v1) claiming method.
If false, returns only jobs that were not claimed via the legacy (v1) claiming method.

inputFields.name: claimed
inputFields.description:
If true, returns only jobs that were claimed via A4A (v2) claiming.
If false, returns only jobs that were not claimed via A4A (v2) claiming.

inputFields.name: hostedJobStatus
inputFields.description: Filter on the hostedJobStatus.

inputFields.name: indeedApplyEnabled
inputFields.description: Boolean filter signifying the presence/absence of an Indeed Apply configuration for this job.

inputFields.name: isCandidatesManagedOnIndeed
inputFields.description: If this filter is set to True, then we will only return jobs where the candidates are managed on Indeed.

inputFields.name: applyMethod
inputFields.description: Filter on the apply method of the job, e.g., it must be applied to at a website, in person, by email, etc.

inputFields.name: indeedApplyEmail
inputFields.description: This filter will return only the jobs that have been configured with the supplied indeedApplyEmail.

inputFields.name: isEditable
inputFields.description: If true, returns only jobs claimed by the calling advertiserId or unclaimed jobs (empty advertiserId).

inputFields.name: isStarred
inputFields.description:
If true, returns only jobs that are in the user's STAR employerJobGroup.
This filter will only work as a 0th or 1st level filter; that is, it will only work unnested
or in a single anyOf or allOf filter. Combinations of anyOfs and allOfs will result in a no-op

inputFields.name: postedBy
inputFields.description: This filter returns jobs posted by the provided account keys (obfuscated account ids using UserTrackingAccountKey)

inputFields.name: postedOrClaimedBy
inputFields.description:
This filter returns jobs posted or claimed by the provided account keys
(obfuscated account ids using UserTrackingAccountKey)

inputFields.name: excludeJobsByEmployerJobIds
inputFields.description: This filter will exclude jobs based on employer job id IRIs.

inputFields.name: employerJobPermission
inputFields.description:
This filter returns jobs wherein the current Employer has the specified permissions.
Currently only READ_CANDIDATES is supported. See EJSEARCH-1196.

inputFields.name: feedId
inputFields.description: This filter returns jobs based on the feedId

inputFields.name: tags
inputFields.description: This filter returns jobs that have the following tags applied (by tagId, also called groupId)

inputFields.name: assignments
inputFields.description: This filter returns jobs that have the following assignments (by groupId)

inputFields.name: isHorizonEnrolled
inputFields.description:
This filter returns jobs that are enrolled in Horizon.
This filter will only work as a 0th or 1st level filter; that is, it will only work unnested
or in a single anyOf or allOf filter. Combinations of anyOfs and allOfs will result in a no-op

inputFields.name: isNexusEnrolled
inputFields.description:
This filter returns jobs that are enrolled in Nexus.
This filter will only work as a 0th or 1st level filter; that is, it will only work unnested
or in a single anyOf or allOf filter. Combinations of anyOfs and allOfs will result in a no-op.
Using this filter within a `not` filter also results in a no-op.

inputFields.name: includeAllNowhereJobs
inputFields.description:
Whether to include all jobs that have their visibility hidden on Indeed (e.g. due to moderation). This filter will
only work as a 0th level filter; it will only work unnested and any usage in a nested expression will be a no-op.

inputFields.name: includeExpiredJobs
inputFields.description:
Whether to include jobs that are recently expired. This filter will only work as a 0th level filter; it will only
work unnested and any usage in a nested expression will be a no-op.

inputFields.name: sponsorshipStatus
inputFields.description:
[In Development: the sponsorshipStatus filter is not yet complete]
Filter on the sponsorship status

inputFields.name: tpiaOnIndeedStatus
inputFields.description:
Filter on a job's TPIA On Indeed status. TPIA On Indeed may also be referred to as Indeed Apply Sync or Candidate Sync.
More information is available at https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/rR3XEQ.

inputFields.name: languageCode

Language code should be a two-letter code indicating the language (ie, "en", "fr").

inputFields.name: filter
inputFields.description:
Filter to find MDP Catalog Entities.

If provided, the filter will be used to find entities matching the specified criteria.

inputFields.name: parameterFilters
inputFields.description:
Advanced parameter-based filters.
If provided, all filters are combined with AND operation.
Each filter consists of a parameter and value pair, with optional exclusion prefix.

inputFields.name: entityTypes
inputFields.description:
Filter by entity type.
Note: This filter is an OR filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values.
If filter option is provided, only entities that match the specified entity type will be returned.
If multiple values are provided, only entities that match ANY of the specified entity types will be returned.

inputFields.name: entityDomains
inputFields.description:
Filter by domain.
Note: This filter is an OR filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values.
If filter option is provided, only entities that match the specified domain will be returned.
If multiple values are provided, only entities that match ANY of the specified domains will be returned.
Note that NONE is a valid domain option.

inputFields.name: dataAvailability
inputFields.description:
"
Filter by data availability.
Note: This filter is an AND filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values, including entities that are not available in online or offline stores.
If ONLINE_AVAILABLE is provided, only entities that are available online will be returned.
If OFFLINE_AVAILABLE is provided, only entities that are available offline will be returned.
If ONLINE_INTEGRATION_AVAILABLE is provided, only entities that are available in online integration store will be returned.
If both ONLINE_AVAILABLE and OFFLINE_AVAILABLE are provided, only entities that are available in both online AND offline stores will be returned.

inputFields.name: entityStage
inputFields.description:
Filter by stage.
Note: This filter is an OR filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values, including stage not set entities.
If filter option is provided, only entities that match the specified stage will be returned.
If multiple values are provided, only entities that match ANY of the specified stages will be returned.

inputFields.name: entityMaturity
inputFields.description:
Filter by maturity.
Note: This filter is an OR filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values.
If filter option is provided, only entities that match the specified maturity option will be returned.
If multiple values are provided, only entities that match ANY of the specified maturity options will be returned.

inputFields.name: entityStatus
inputFields.description:
Filter by entity status.
Note: This filter is an OR filter.

If filter option is null or empty, it will match all possible values.
If filter option is provided, only entities that match the specified status option will be returned.
If multiple values are provided, only entities that match ANY of the specified status options will be returned.

types.name: FindWorkedShiftsSubjectFilter
types.description:
Filter to allow finding WorkedShifts with flexibility to:
- return WORKER versions if exists, else nothing
- return WORKER versions if exists, else CLIENT if exists
- return CLIENT versions if exists, else nothing
- return CLIENT versions if exists, else WORKER if exists
- return WORKER and CLIENT versions

The default behavior for querying for WorkedShifts across the platform is to:
- try to find the requested subject (e.g. WORKER)
- if it doesn't exist, try to find the other subject (e.g. CLIENT)
So conceptually:
- querying for WorkedShifts as a Worker should probably filter by WORKER_ELSE_CLIENT
- querying for WorkedShifts as a Client should probably filter by CLIENT_ELSE_WORKER

types.name: GroupedAnalyticsMetricData
types.description:
Represents the result of a grouped metrics query, providing a structured overview of
the metrics grouped by specified dimensions. This type encapsulates the title,
description, dimensions, metrics, data, and insights for the grouped metrics report.
It is designed to facilitate the analysis of performance or behavior across different
categories or attributes, making it suitable for visualizations and detailed reporting.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
Title of the grouped metrics report, providing a concise summary of the
report's focus or purpose. This title is intended to give users a quick
understanding of what the report covers, such as "Engagement Metrics by Region"
or "Sales Performance by Product Category".

fields.name: description
fields.description:
Description of the grouped metrics report, offering detailed context and
background information about the metrics being analyzed. This description
helps users understand the significance of the metrics, the dimensions used,
and the overall objectives of the report. It may include explanations of
the dimensions and metrics, the time period covered, and any specific
methodologies or considerations relevant to the analysis.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.description:
Dimensions used to group the metrics data. These dimensions provide
context for the metrics, allowing for segmented analysis across different
categories or attributes. For example, dimensions could include time periods,
geographic locations, user segments, or any other relevant categorical data.

fields.name: groupingEligibleDimensions
fields.description:
A list of dimension IDs that are eligible for grouping and can be sent as input
when querying grouped metrics. This list defines which dimensions can be used
for grouping the metrics data.

fields.name: metrics
fields.description:
Metrics that are calculated based on the grouped dimensions. Each metric
represents a specific quantitative measure, such as totals, averages, or
counts, that are relevant to the grouped dimensions. These metrics are
designed to provide insights into the performance or behavior of the
dimensions being analyzed.

fields.name: data
fields.description:
Data for the metrics, grouped by dimensions. This is suitable for
visualizations like segmented bar graphs, heatmaps, or multi-dimensional
analyses where each group of dimensions provides a unique perspective on the metrics.

types.name: GroupedAnalyticsMetricsData
types.description:
Represents the data for grouped metrics, including dimensions and metrics. This type is used to encapsulate the
grouped metrics data returned by the `data` field in the `GroupedAnalyticsMetricData`.
This structure allows for a clear organization of the dimensions and metrics associated with each group,
making it suitable for visualizations and detailed analysis.

types.name: GroupedAnalyticsMetricsDataConnection
types.description:
A connection type that provides pagination for grouped metrics data.
This connection allows clients to retrieve a subset of grouped metrics data
based on the specified pagination parameters, such as `after`, `first`, `before`, and `last`.
This structure is useful for efficiently handling large datasets and enabling clients to navigate through the results.

types.name: GroupedAnalyticsMetricsDataEdge
types.description:
An edge in the grouped metrics data connection, representing a single
group of dimensions and their associated metrics data.
This edge contains a `node` that holds the grouped metrics data and a `cursor`
that can be used for pagination.

types.name: GroupedAnalyticsMetricsInput
types.description:
Defines the input parameters for retrieving grouped analytics metrics data.
This input type allows consumers to specify which metrics report to retrieve,
how to group the metrics data, how to filter the data, and how to sort the results.
It provides a comprehensive way to customize analytics queries to meet specific
reporting and visualization needs.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description:
The unique identifier of the metrics report to retrieve.
This determines which predefined set of metrics and dimensions will be available
in the response.

inputFields.name: groupByDimensions
inputFields.description:
A list of dimension IDs by which to group the metrics data.
When provided, metrics will be calculated separately for each unique combination
of the specified dimensions. For example, grouping by ["campaign", "job-country"]
would calculate metrics for each unique campaign and country combination.


The dimensions specified must be from the list of available groupingEligibleDimensions
returned in the GroupedAnalyticsMetricsData.

inputFields.name: filter
inputFields.description:
Filtering criteria to apply to the metrics data.
This field is required and must include at least a dateRange.
Additional field filters can be applied to narrow the results further.

inputFields.name: sort
inputFields.description:
Optional sorting criteria for the result set.
Allows sorting by dimensions or metrics in ascending or descending order.
When multiple sort inputs are provided, they are applied in sequence
(first sort by the first criterion, then by the second to break ties, etc.).

types.name: HiringEventSchedulingChoice
types.description:
This corresponds to the scheduling choices available for a job seeker seeking an interview.
There are 5 cases for how this data may be represented:
* The event does not use timeslots and has no max for RSVPs
* The event does not use timeslots and has an event max for RSVPs
* The event uses timeslots and has no max for RSVPs
* The event uses timeslots and has an event max for RSVPs
* The event uses timeslots and has a RSVP max per timeslot

fields.name: timePeriod
fields.description:
Period of time available.
This field can be represented through event timeslots or event sessions depending on if the event uses timeslots.

fields.name: remainingCapacity
fields.description:
How many more people can be schedule into the time period. There are 3 cases for what this field will represent:
* When this field is null, there is no RSVP max capacity for the event or timeslot if timeslots are used
* When the event uses timeslots and has timeslot RSVP max, this field represents the capacity remaining for this slot

There is a limit imposed on how many hiring journeys can be returned at once, which depends on which hiring journey fields
are selected by the query.

If the selections are limited to only the hiring journey's "id", "lastModified", and the linked

fields.name: hiringJourneyCount
fields.description:
If isHiringJourneyCountMinimum is false, hiringJourneyCount represents the total number of hiring journeys that would be on
this connection if we were to fetch them all.

If isHiringJourneyCountMinimum is true, hiringJourneyCount represents a minimum count of hiring journeys that would be on
this connection if we were to fetch them all. The true number of hiring journeys is equal to or greater than this count.

The expectation should be that small counts are precise while large counts are a minimum. This is a practical
compromise because counting large numbers of hiring journeys can be an expensive operation.

Certain indeed-internal clients can use this to get all the attributes for an HJP.
Non-internal clients will get an error if they request this field.
Internal clients that are not specifically permitted to use this field will simply get a copy of whatever they requested

fields.name: nullableAttributes
fields.description:
This field is equivalent to attributes with the exception that it is nullable.
If a query is made with insufficient permissions to access a particular field, the response sets that field to null and returns the rest.
However, if that field is not nullable, the null bubbles up to the closest nullable field. In the case where attributes are requested,
this means that HostedJob itself will return null.
To get around that, use nullableAttributes in a query that will be used for users with or without Hosted_Job/Read perms.

types.name: InboundCandidateSyncError
types.description: Error codes that may be encountered during Inbound Candidate Sync

enumValues.name: UNKNOWN
enumValues.description: An unrecognized/unclassified error

enumValues.name: INVALID_PROFILE
enumValues.description: The candidate/application in the ATS/CRM was missing data required for transfer to Indeed

enumValues.name: AUTHORIZATION
enumValues.description: A permissions error occurred while transferring the candidate/application

enumValues.name: DESERIALIZATION
enumValues.description:
Some portions of the candidate/application were discarded due to being in an unknown/unsupported format that could
not be converted to Indeed data

enumValues.name: PRECONDITION
enumValues.description: Some prerequisite of import candidate or application publishing failed

enumValues.name: PUBLISHING_CANDIDATE_SUBMISSION
enumValues.description: Publishing a candidate submission to UCP failed

enumValues.name: PUBLISHING_RAW_DISPOSITION
enumValues.description: The application's disposition data (as defined by the ATS/CRM) failed to sync to Indeed

enumValues.name: PUBLISHING_QUESTION_ANSWERS
enumValues.description: The candidate/application's question and/or answer data failed to sync to Indeed

enumValues.name: PUBLISHING_NORMALIZED_DISPOSITION
enumValues.description: The application's normalized disposition data could not be synced to Indeed

enumValues.name: VIRUS_SCAN_NOT_COMPLETED
enumValues.description: Virus scanning was not run / failed to complete for a file, causing it to be discarded

enumValues.name: VIRUS_SCAN_FAILED
enumValues.description: Virus scanning a file flagged it as potentially unsafe, causing it to be discarded

enumValues.name: ALL_FILES_NOT_IMPORTED
enumValues.description:
Not all files from the ATS could be stored on Indeed
Typically, this means more than one resume and cover letter were present, since only one of each can be saved

enumValues.name: ALL_ATS_FIELDS_NOT_IMPORTED
enumValues.description: Some fields were set in the ATS that could not be mapped to an Indeed field

enumValues.name: RESUME_PARSING
enumValues.description: Resume parsing or one of its subtasks (e.g. model conversion) failed

enumValues.name: ALL_QUESTIONS_ANSWERS_NOT_IMPORTED
enumValues.description:
One or more questions or answers were not imported to Indeed. This could be due to a question being flagged as
collecting demographic data, or the question type being unsupported.

enumValues.name: PERIPHERAL_IDENTITY_NOT_CREATED
enumValues.description: A peripheral identity could not be created or retrieved for the Jobseeker.

enumValues.name: PERIPHERAL_IDENTITY_INVALID_EMAIL
enumValues.description: The email address of the Jobseeker is invalid.

fields.name: initialize
fields.description:
Initializes (or re-initializes) sync progress for a connection, type, and external location. The result of this
operation is that current and backfill sync positions will be reset to the `initializationPositionAt` timestamp. If
a new sync progress is being inserted, current sync position and backfill position timestamps will be set to the
value of `initializationPositionAt`. Attempting to initialize a new sync progress document that already exists will
return the existing document without modification.

fields.name: update
fields.description:
Updates an existing sync progress for a connection, type, and external location. `initializationUpdatedAt` is expected
to be provided on all update requests to prevent out of sync modification of sync progress documents between services.
Either 'currentSyncPositionAt' or 'currentBackfillPositionAt' must be provided.

types.description:
Rules that specify when an [Calendar] is potentially available for
events to be scheduled.

types.name: IncludePeriodInput
types.description: Input for creating include availability time periods.

inputFields.name: key
inputFields.description:
The String that uniquely identifies the available period within a calendar configuration.
The first request made for an Id will create an available period for the account and subsequent requests will update its details.
Usually this will be an internal ID for the available period, encoded as an ASCII-only String of up to 64 characters.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description: Start time of the rule period. Resolution is 1 minute. Any sub-minute portion of the value is dropped.

inputFields.name: endTime
inputFields.description: End time of the rule period. Value must be greater than [startTime]. Resolution is 1 minute. Any sub-minute portion of the value is dropped.

inputFields.name: maxWeight
inputFields.description:
maxWeight is ONE measure of the 'capacity' of this period. The weight for a period is the sum of all weights of appointments occurring during that time range.
Appointments can be booked for this period only while the period weight (including the new appointment) is less than or equal to the maxWeight.
In most cases, this value should be thought of as the number of humans conducting this interview. For 1:1 cases, this value should be 1.0 since there is only one human. For back-to-back cases where there could be multiple humans conducting appointments concurrently, this value could be > 1.0.
This value is NOT meant to be the same as an RSVP Cap. Please reach out to the S&A team if you have any questions.
The maxWeight must be greater than 0.0 and must be 1.0 for user calendar configurations. This value will only be used for Include Periods and should not be set on Exclude Periods.

inputFields.name: screenerQuestions
inputFields.description: The screener questions are a list of general, well-formatted questions that pertain to the underlying job, such as work experience, skills, certifications, and so on. This list cannot contain demographic questions, such as question about ethnicity, gender, or disability. Certain jurisdictions regulate questions related to *protected classes* of people. Indeed systems, and potentially your systems, must handle these questions in special ways.

inputFields.name: demographicQuestions
inputFields.description:
The demographic questions are a list of specific, well-formatted questions that pertain to the job applicant's *protected class*. That is, ethnicity, gender, disability, and so on. Certain jurisdictions must regulate these questions. Indeed systems, and potentially your systems, must handle these questions in special ways. 

These questions are limited to U.S.-based jobs for EEO compliance.

Do not include general screener questions, such as those that pertain to work experience, skills, or certifications, in this list. Instead place them in the `screenerQuestions` list.

1) Employer has viewed at least one application

Returns 'false' otherwise.

fields.description:
An adjusted measure of the probability that the employer will respond to job applications for a specific job.
Uses different time thresholds (7 days for no action, 21 days for not viewed) compared to employerReplyLikelihood.
For now, this will be either 'RESPONSE_LIKELY', 'RESPONSE_UNLIKELY', 'REVIEWING_OTHERS', or 'UNKNOWN' as default.

types.name: InterviewConnectionAction
types.description:
actions specific to products that need to distinguish between
arrival (when a person showed) vs. joining (when a person
is able to start a specific interview connection).

In a happy path where the jobseeker and interviewer
connect in a hosted video interview, all of the following
InterviewConnectionActions are expected: JOBSEEKER_ARRIVED,
JOBSEEKER_JOINED, INTERVIEWER_ARRIVED, INTERVIEWER_JOINED,
CONNECTION_STARTED, JOBSEEKER_LEFT, INTERVIEWER_LEFT,
CONNECTION_ENDED

enumValues.name: DEFAULT
enumValues.description:
DEFAULT should never be used, but is required to ensure a known
value exists to identify breaking changes in our
protobuf schema

enumValues.name: JOBSEEKER_JOINED
enumValues.description:
the jobseeker joined the interview - note that for hosted
interviews, this is not the same thing as the jobseeker arriving

enumValues.name: JOBSEEKER_LEFT
enumValues.description: the jobseeker left the interview

enumValues.name: INTERVIEWER_JOINED
enumValues.description:
the employer joined the interview - note that for hosted video
interviews, this is not the same thing as the employer arriving

enumValues.name: INTERVIEWER_LEFT
enumValues.description: the employer left the interview

enumValues.name: CONNECTION_ATTEMPT_ENDED
enumValues.description: interview ended without a connection

enumValues.name: CONNECTION_STARTED
enumValues.description:
the connection started, this will almost always
be accompanied by another action (e.g. JOBSEEKER_JOINED or
INTERVIEWER_JOINED)

enumValues.name: CONNECTION_ENDED
enumValues.description:
the connection ended, this should always result
In the connection duration being updated and will almost always be
accompanied by another action (e.g. JOBSEEKER_LEFT or INTERVIEWER_LEFT)

enumValues.name: JOBSEEKER_ARRIVED
enumValues.description:
JOBSEEKER_ARRIVED represents the action of a jobseeker
arriving to the interview location, but they may not be able to
connect with an interviewer yet.
In hosted video, this is when the jobseeker has entered the lobby,
but has not entered a convo room. In IRL events,
this is when the jobseeker arrives to the event, but before they
have spoken with an interviewer (wait time).

enumValues.name: INTERVIEWER_ARRIVED
enumValues.description:
INTERVIEWER_ARRIVED represents the action of a interviewer
arriving to the interview location, but they may not be able to
connect with the jobseeker for the specific interview yet.
In hosted video, this is when the interviewer
has entered the lobby, but has not entered the convo room related
to the ICR's related IMP interview.
In IRL events, this is when the interviewer arrives to the event,
but before they have spoken with this jobseeker (wait time).

enumValues.name: DEFAULT
enumValues.description:
DEFAULT should never be used, but is required
to ensure a known value exists to identify breaking changes in
our protobufs

enumValues.name: NO_INFORMATION
enumValues.description: Neither jobseeker nor any interviewers have reported show data

enumValues.name: ONE_PARTY_REPORTED
enumValues.description:
Only one of the employer(s) or jobseeker has reported show data.
See the interviewConnectionActions enum for granular reports.

enumValues.name: CONFLICTING_INFORMATION
enumValues.description:
The employer and jobseeker have reported conflicting show data.
See the interviewConnectionActions enum for granular reports.

enumValues.name: PENDING
enumValues.description:
The interview is in progress, and at least one participant has
joined, but the jobseeker has not connected with an interviewer
yet.

enumValues.name: INTERVIEWING
enumValues.description:
The interview is in progress, and the jobseeker is currently
connecting with an interviewer.

enumValues.name: INTERVIEWED
enumValues.description:
The interview was completed, and the jobseeker connected
with at least one interviewer.

enumValues.name: EMPLOYER_NO_SHOW
enumValues.description: The interview has ended, and the jobseeker showed, but all interviewers were no-shows.

enumValues.name: JOBSEEKER_NO_SHOW
enumValues.description:
The interview has ended, and the interviewer showed, but the
jobseeker no showed.

enumValues.name: MUTUAL_NO_SHOW
enumValues.description: The interview has ended, and neither party showed.

enumValues.name: MISSED_CONNECTION
enumValues.description:
The interview has ended, and both parties showed, but did not
connect.

fields.name: attributes
fields.description:
**Example:**

Get attributes for job types or remote as a separate field

```
jobTypes: attributes ( keys: ["DSQF7"] customClass: "BM62A" ) {
  key
  label
}
```

args.name: keys
args.description:
Restrict attributes by specified [SUID](https://wiki.indeed.com/display/MetadataTaxonomy/Glossary+and+Terminology#GlossaryandTerminology-SUID) keys.
If multiple keys and/or customClass are provided, attributes matching at least one key/customClass are returned.
If no keys and customClass are provided, all attributes are returned.

Example: "DSQF7" (Remote)

args.name: customClass
args.description:
Provide a [custom class](https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MetadataTaxonomy/pages/215485397/Classes) SUID to restrict which attributes are returned.

Example: "BM62A" (Job Type)

args.name: sources
args.description: If specified, the returned attributes will be restricted to the given sources.

fields.name: defaultAttributes
fields.description: Get all attributes for the job.

args.name: occupationOption
args.description:
Optional, Includes MOST_SPECIFIC and WITH_ANCESTORS, MOST_LIKELY (deprecated) will be treated as MOST_SPECIFIC
Please do not use TOP_LEVEL(deprecated), it will be treated as MOST_SPECIFIC
WITH_ANCESTORS will be the default if not provided.
When filter for EMPLOYER provided occupations, be sure to provide BOTH occupationOption and JobOccupationSource
because default source is EXTRACTED if not provided

args.name: sources
args.description:
If specified, the returned occupations will be restricted to the given sources.
If nothing provided, default is EXTRACTED

args.name: customClass
args.description:
Provide a [custom class](https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MetadataTaxonomy/pages/215485397/Classes) SUID to restrict which occupations are returned.

Example: "CMF3G" (Indeed Occupation)

fields.name: formattedText
fields.description:
Text summary of complete salary data. E.g. `$15 - $21 an hour`, `$55,000 a
year`, and so on. The content is localized via the `locale` HTTP request
parameter. E.g. `$12 - $13 por hora` when `locale=es-US`.

Note also that the country part of the locale has to match the currency of
the salary data represented by `key`. E.g. `US` matches `USD` and `JP`
matches `JPY`. In the case of a mismatch the `JobCompensation` would be
`null`.

fields.description:

"contact": the primary contact information for the job, including where applications should be sent
"hiring manager": hiring manager
"recruiter": recruiter
"user": other users, such as interviewers or coordinators

Example: this contact is the primary contact of the job and is also the recruiter, returns ["contact", "recruiter"]
fields.deprecationReason: contact types will no longer be returned due to JRS-2178

fields.name: contactEmail
fields.description:
Email address of the contact for the job.

Example: "ab123456@gmail.com"
fields.deprecationReason: contact email will no longer be returned due to JRS-2178

fields.name: contactName
fields.description:
Optional name for the client's contact

Example: "John Lee"
fields.deprecationReason: contact name will no longer be returned due to JRS-2178

fields.name: contactPhone
fields.description:
Optional phone number of the contact
Data source: jobTags

Example: "11294013391"

Full definition can be found here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ubfjXB2c_OPuoIP7qnH2cRF7r9y5_XlH-vFvjL_j27k/edit#heading=h.f8t70hc12nof

enumValues.name: REPOST
enumValues.description: The request job is a copy of another job that is no longer "live"

enumValues.name: DUPLICATE
enumValues.description: The request job is a copy of another job that is currently "live"

enumValues.name: PRE_AGGREGATION_COPY
enumValues.description: The request job is a copy of another job that has not gone through the aggregation process yet. ie. the copied job was created very recently

enumValues.name: UNKNOWN
enumValues.description: copy type could not be determined

Apollo client needs an identifier field to normalize cache object
and auto-merge fields, otherwise avoidable network requests
or even infinite loops could happen

you should always request the id field when it's available

ideally, it should be stable and never change
see https://docs.google.com/document/d/10OtH7yoB-P8LQHarD-tkdJLo8ogbZsxKSldeRHTk_vY/edit

and employerJobId for EmployerJob

fields.name: tmpSurface
fields.description:
A surface is platform that hosts a searchable
set of job posts to a job seeker.
For the MVP, we will only expose “INDEED” surface ID visibility
NOTE:
  We use tmpSurface as there is a current proposal to create
  standardized surface IDs:
  SurfaceId (AdFormat Alternative) Design Review
  When the standard is adopted, tmpSurface will be deprecated
  and replaced with `surfaceId` using the widely accepted IDs.
We could in the future provide more granularity

fields.name: isSearchable
fields.description:
Is this job visible for job search on this surface?
For more details on why this job is not searchable, refer to
the messaging tags (TODO: upcoming field on
JobSearchSurfaceStatus).

fields.name: isViewable
fields.description: Is this job viewable? I.e. can user get a direct link to view the job?

fields.name: isSponsorshipRequired
fields.description:
Requires sponsorship to be searchable on this surface.
Typically only relevant to Indeed-hosted surfaces. Other surfaces
would not require sponsorship or sponsorship is not a feature on
on these surfaces.

fields.name: isSponsorshipApplied
fields.description: Is this job sponsored and the sponsorship propagated to the index service

fields.name: isSponsorshipTargeted
fields.description:
Is this job added to a campaign but may not have propagated to the index service, if the Employer Job is an indexed job this would return null
This field reflects both dradis single and multiple sponsorship

fields.name: isMissingRequiredSponsorship
fields.description: Is this job rejected due to it not having sponsorship applied or targeted

fields.name: targetedSponsorshipCampaigns

Null if isSponsorshipTargeted is false or null

types.description: Options for getting the jobscore

inputFields.name: versionOverride
inputFields.description: Override the Job Score version. If not set, the default version will be used (currently v0).

inputFields.name: jobInputs
inputFields.description:
Override the fields used for computing the score for draft jobs. This will apply to all queried draft jobs.
Please contact #job-optimization if other use cases are needed.

inputFields.name: variantOverrides
inputFields.description:
Overrides for the variants of optimizations.
A variant is an alternative implementation of an optimization: the backend may potentially calculate the value of
each field in the response differently depending on the variant.
If left unspecified, the default variant will be used.

inputFields.name: clientApp
inputFields.description:
The name of the app which is calling this endpoint.
Specify whatever string you'd like to query Job Optimization indices with.
If this field is omitted, we default to use a value built from OneGraph request headers:
"indeed-fed-client-sub-app" and "indeed-fed-client-sub-app-component".

types.name: JobScoreOptimization
types.description: Actually want to implement PossibleJobOptimization but can't due to restrictions in Apollo federation version

fields.name: optType
fields.description: Optimization type.

fields.name: potentialScore
fields.description: Score for the optimization which ranges from 0.0 to 1.0. All potential scores should sum to the overallScore

fields.name: hiddenBy
fields.description:
If set, it indicates that this optimization is hidden by another optimization. The value will be the name of another
optimization type, such as 'exists_salary', and the corresponding optimization type will always be present in the
list of optimizations in the JobOptimizationJobScore object for this job in this response.
The UI should not normally show a hidden optimization to the user. If the optimization type corresponding to
"hiddenBy" is accepted, award the job score for both optimizations, and log both optimizations as accepted.
This will be deprecated soon. Use hiddenByOptType instead.

list of optimizations in the JobOptimizationJobScore object for this job in this response.
The UI should not normally show a hidden optimization to the user. If the optimization type corresponding to
"hiddenBy" is accepted, award the job score for both optimizations, and log both optimizations as accepted.

Whether this boolean filter MUST or MUST NOT match. MUST is the positive filtering while MUST NOT is negative.
Default is MUST.

fields.name: min
fields.description:
The minimum value of this range (inclusive lower bound).
In the first range this value is null, and in other ranges it is identical to `max` in the previous range.

fields.name: max
fields.description:
The minimum value of this range (exclusive upper bound).
In the last range this value is null, and in other ranges it is identical to `min` in the next range.

fields.name: count
fields.description: The count of jobs whose values of base salary are in this range.

fields.name: currencyCode
fields.description: [ISO 4217](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217) currency code

fields.name: baseAnnualSalary
fields.description:
Best available salary in local currency, sourced from extracted salary, estimated salary or override values.

The returned list consists of ranges of salary which are dynamically determined from the distribution of salary.
These ranges are distinct and sorted.
The number of returned ranges is at most `maxNumRanges` but may be smaller depending on the distribution.

**Note:** It is prohibited to request multiple `baseAnnualSalary` facets in a single search request.

args.name: maxNumRanges
args.description: Maximum number of ranges to be returned. This must be between 1 and 50, inclusive.

args.name: minRangeWidth
args.description: The shortest possible width (i.e., `max` - `min`) of each range. Some default value is used if this is not provided.

types.name: JobSearchCompositeFilterInput

inputFields.name: filters
inputFields.description:
A list of filters to be combined with the specified operation.

- Supported filter types are keyword and composite.  If any other types are used then a fatal error will be returned.
- For each filter in the list, it must only contain one type of filter (e.g. only keyword or only composite).  If there are multiple types then a fatal error will be returned.
- There can't be more that 99 levels of nested filters, otherwise a fatal error will be returned.

inputFields.name: operation
inputFields.description: The way `filters` will be joined. Default is AND.

fields.name: endTime

types.name: JobSearchDateFacetIntervalInput
types.description:
Defines an interval to request job counts for

**Warning:** invalid format of start/end values will result in a invalid request error

inputFields.name: label
inputFields.description: Label to be used in `JobSearchDateFacet` related response (e.g., "Last Day", "Last 3 Days", "LAST_DAY")

inputFields.name: start
inputFields.description:
Specify the start (inclusive lower bound) of the interval. Format is "{number of days}d" OR "{number of hours}h"

Values are relative to now. For example "1d" represents exactly 24 hours before now.

Value must be "older" than that of `end` (e.g., if `end` is "7d" `start` must be at least "8d")

**Examples:**
- "6h"
- "1d"
- "7d"
- "14d"

**Default:** null (aka "beginning of time")

inputFields.name: end
inputFields.description:
Specify the end (exclusive upper bound) of the interval. Format is "{number of days}d" OR "{number of hours}h"

Values are relative to now. For example "1d" represents exactly 24 hours before now.

Value must be "newer" than that of `start` (e.g., if `start` is "7d" `end` must be at least "6d")

**Examples:**
- "6h"
- "1d"
- "7d"
- "14d"

**Default:** null (aka "now", "0d", "0h")

types.name: JobSearchFacets
types.description:
A collection of search facets.

Useful for retrieving the number of job in the overall result set that match a certain criteria (e.g., number of
jobs new to Indeed in the last 7 days).

Reference: [Faceted Search](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faceted_search)

fields.name: dateOnIndeed
fields.description: Provides facets related to the `Job.dateOnIndeed` field

args.name: intervals
args.description: Requests must include at least 1 interval and are limited to a maximum of 50

fields.name: attributes
fields.description:
Provides facets resulted to the `Job.attributes` field

Results are in descending order based on the `count`

It is valid to specify any combination of the `top`, `keys`, and `customClass` fields. There result will be the
union of all attributes matched by each field's behaviour

**Examples:**
- `top:5 customClass: "BM62A"` will return the top 5 most common attributes under the specified customClass.
- `top:5 customClass: "BM62A" keys: [ "CF3CP", "75GKK" ]` will return the top 5 attributes under customClass "BM62A" AND well as counts for keys "CF3CP" and "75GKK".

**Use case:** remote jobs faceting
Currently, we support 2 SUIDs for remote jobs:
- "DSQF7": Remote (A job that can be performed entirely remotely. May involve on-site training or an on-site interview.)
- "VAMUB": Temporarily remote (COVID-19)

Please use them for remote jobs faceting. Example:
```
facets {
  remote: attributes ( keys: [ "DSQF7", "VAMUB"] ) {
    key
    label
    count
  }
}
```

You can also use these SUIDs in the keyword filter with field name "attributes". Example:
```
filters: [
  {
    keyword: {
      field: "attributes"
      keys: ["DSQF7"]
    }
  }
]
```

args.name: top
args.description:
Return the top most frequent job attributes contained in the result set up to the number requested.

Defaults to 5 if `keys` is null or empty; 0 otherwise.
Must be at least 1 and at most 25 when specified.

See `customClass`

args.name: keys
args.description:
Return facets for each of the specified [SUID](https://wiki.indeed.com/display/MetadataTaxonomy/Glossary+and+Terminology#GlossaryandTerminology-SUID) keys.

Will return counts for all specificed keys.
Keys are limited to a maximum 25.

Note: no validation is made on keys

args.name: customClass
args.description:
Used to restrict `top` job attributes to the specified custom class. For example return the top 5 job types
(customClass: "BM62A").

Note: no validation is made on value. If `customClass` does not exist 0 facets will be returned

**Supported Values:**
- BM62A : Job Types
- YYMAS : Contract Types

fields.name: compensation
glassdoor
fields.description: Provides facets related to the Glassdoor fields

fields.name: occupations
fields.description:
Provides facets resulted to the `Job.occupations` field

Results are in descending order based on the `count`

It is valid to specify any combination of the `top` and `keys` fields.
There result will be the union of all occupations matched by each field's behaviour

**Examples:**
- `top:5 keys: [ "C3XKZ", "KNBYF" ]` will return the top 5 occupations as well as counts for keys "C3XKZ" and "KNBYF".

You can also use these SUIDs in the keyword filter with field name "occupations". Example:
```
filters: [
  {
    keyword: {
      field: "occupations"
      keys: ["C3XKZ"]
    }
  }
]
```

args.name: top

|occupations|UUID or SUID|
|attributes|UUID or SUID|

|jobKey|The same format as `Job/key`|
|location.city|Combination of admin codes and city formatted by location.city facets|

|transit.company.key|Transit company key|
|transit.line.key|Transit line key|
|transit.station.key|Transit station key|

|glassdoor.employerKey|Glassdoor employer key|
|glassdoor.industryKey|(Deprecated, use industryNKey) Glassdoor industry key|

fields.name: graphEmbedding
fields.description:
Job seeker graph embedding feature, built by the Indeed Knowledge Graph team using GNN for enhanced similarity search.
The input to the GNN model consists of edges between jobs, job seekers and companies.
Given a target node and the sub-graph contains the node, the GNN model calculates the embedding of the target node
following the steps below.
1. Encode each entity using the same entity encoders as those used in the baseline model. The encoder used for
companies is quite similar to the encoders used for jobs or job seekers.
2. For each type of path or meta-path, aggregate the source nodes by averaging their entity encodings.
3. Project the features obtained from step 2, using different weights for different types of paths or meta-paths.
4. Use a transformer to fuse the features obtained from step 3.

Wiki: https://wiki.indeed.com/display/MetadataTaxonomy/Graph+Neural+Network+Embeddings

types.name: JobSeekerProfileLocationType
types.description: A Job Seeker's location details.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The street-level address inputted by the user. Other location fields may have been extracted by the Profile Precise Geoocoder from this street address.

fields.name: address2
fields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's street address line 2. This could be an unit number.

fields.name: admin1
fields.description: The highest level of administrative division for a given market (e.g. state in US, region in JP, country in GB, etc.). The value may have been written by the location geocoder service based on the user-input unknownLocation field.

fields.name: admin2
fields.description: The second highest level of administrative division for a given market (e.g. county in US, prefecture in JP, etc.). The value may have been written by the location geocoder service based on the user-input unknownLocation field.

fields.name: admin3
fields.description: The third highest level of administrative division for a given market. Only used in some markets. The value may have been written by the location geocoder service based on the user-input unknownLocation field.

fields.name: admin4
fields.description: The fourth highest level of administrative division for a given market. Only used in some markets. The value may have been written by the location geocoder service based on the user-input unknownLocation field.

fields.name: geocodePrecision
fields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's geocode precision, e.g. COUNTRY or CITY. This value is generated by the location geocoding service based on user-input fields in the location.

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's latitude. When the geocode precision is postal or larger, the coordinates are typically the approximate centroid of the area.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's longitude. When the geocode precision is postal or larger, the coordinates are typically the approximate centroid of the area.

fields.name: state
fields.description: This field is deprecated, please use admin1 instead.

fields.name: unknownLocation
fields.description: A user-inputted value representing Job Seeker's raw location input used for location geocoding. This field is labeled as "City, State" or "City" depending on country. An example value is "Albany, New York". Other location fields including admin1, admin2, admin3, admin4, city, country, latitude, longitude, and geocode precision were likely extracted from this field by the location geocoder service.

fields.name: formattedLocation
fields.description: The formatted location to display in City field in profile UI. For US locations, this field will have format "City, State" and for other countries it will be just "City". Note the city will appear in the canonical language defined in the location database.  Since location translations are not supported, the unknownLocation (the raw user input) will be displayed if the browser locale doesn't match the location country.

fields.name: fullFormattedLocation
fields.description: The fully formatted location, structured based on market-specific requirements. In general, it encompasses city, administrative divisions, and postal code. This can be used in situations where the underlying logic behind the format of formattedLocation doesn't meet a specific client's needs

fields.name: admin1Name
fields.description: This is the name corresponding to the admin1 field. eg. for 'MH' admin1, the admin1Name is 'Maharashtra'.

fields.name: admin2Name
fields.description: This is the name corresponding to the admin2 field. eg. for '6619347' admin2, the admin2Name is 'Navi Mumbai District'.

fields.name: admin3Name
fields.description: This is the name corresponding to the admin3 field. eg. for 'NVM' admin3, the admin3Name is 'Navi Mumbai'.

fields.name: admin4Name
fields.description: This is the name corresponding to the admin4 field. eg. for '270075' admin4, the admin4Name is 'Ghansoli'.

inputFields.name: address
inputFields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's street address.  Street address is not used by geocoding in this service but is geocoded by a different process.

inputFields.name: address2
inputFields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's street address line 2. This could be an unit number.

inputFields.name: admin1
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's admin1. In some countries, this is the state or provenance.

inputFields.name: admin2
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's admin2

inputFields.name: admin3
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's admin3

inputFields.name: admin4
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's admin4

inputFields.name: city
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's canonical city name as defined in Location Service.  Note the language might not match the browser locale or the city entered by the job seeker.

inputFields.name: country
inputFields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's country.  Do not set this to the browser locale country since the Job Seeker's location might not match the browser locale.

inputFields.name: geocodePrecision
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's geocode precision which has a value like COUNTRY or CITY. This value should only be provided if the location has already been geocoded by location geocoding service or a similar service and includes all the geocoded fields defined in this location type are present in input.

inputFields.name: latitude
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's latitude

inputFields.name: location
inputFields.description: This is a deprecated location field that should not be used.

inputFields.name: longitude
inputFields.description: A geocoded value representing a Job Seeker's longitude

inputFields.name: postalCode
inputFields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's postal code

inputFields.name: state
inputFields.description: This field is deprecated, please use admin1 instead.

inputFields.name: unknownLocation
inputFields.description: A user inputted value representing Job Seeker's raw location input used for location geocoding. This field is labeled as "City, State" or "City" depending on country.  An example value is "Albany, New York". The location geocoder service will attempt to extract admin1, admin2, admin3, admin4, city, country, latitude, longitude, and geocode precision from this field. Typically, the client should include unknown location, country, address, address2, and postal code fields and rely on profile-graphql to geocode the location. An exception is location geocoder service which will write already geocode latitude, longitude, and geocodePrecision. For more information about how location geocoding works go to https://wiki.indeed.com/display/PROF/Profile+Location+Geocoding.

fields.name: updateSourcingElection
fields.description:
Sets the sourcing election of an account. This controls whether or not employers can view the job seeker's
  resume/profile. As such, this is considered important for our high fidelity concerns.
  
Updates the resume state as part of the same call, so services that rely on that field will still show the
  proper state. This mutation should be preferred to alternatives for this reason. It's especially discouraged
  to make a separate call from a client environment.
  
If the account has been locked out by moderators, this mutation will fail with a PGAPI_E-004 error
  (PERMISSION DENIED)

fields.name: updateSourcingElectionForAccount
fields.description:
This mutation performs all the same functionality of the updateSourcingElection mutation however it is intended to be
used only from internal tools, such as modtools, that update account privacy on behalf of the jobseeker.

inputFields.name: customClassSuids
inputFields.description:
By default (if customClassSuids is null or empty) all attributes will be returned and grouped by fundamental classes.
Fundamental class in YellowHat: https://yellowhat.sandbox.indeed.net/#/version/production/7e116979-c310-47f8-af81-0443dc4d5cbc
If a list of custom class suids is provided, the attributes will be grouped and filtered on these custom classes.
For example: customClassSuids: ["SXMYH"] will return positive and negative attributes only belonging to Benefits class

fields.name: positivePreferenceAttributesByCustomClass
fields.description: Positive preference attributes grouped by custom class. Each item in the list corresponds to a different custom class for example Occupational Specialty or Benefit and a list of taxonomy attributes that belong to each custom class.

fields.name: negativePreferenceAttributesByCustomClass
fields.description: Negative preference attributes grouped by custom class. Also known as disliked preferences. Each item in the list corresponds to a different custom class for example Occupational Specialty or Benefit and a list of taxonomy attributes that belong to each custom class.

fields.name: template
fields.description:
Template string (with tokens denoted by "[]" that will be replaced
with placeholder values). For example: "Took care of approximately [number of] [patient type] patients daily"
In this example, two placeholder objects would also return with the payload:
one for "number of" (which would have no associated options, since it's free input)
and another for "patient type" (which would have a list of options like "elderly" or "hospice")

fields.name: placeholders
fields.description:
Array of placeholder objects (sorted in order of their associated
appearance in the template string)

fields.name: options
fields.description:
Array of options that could be swapped in place of the token
(an empty array if the placeholder is free input). For example, if the
template string included a token like "[number of]", this would be an empty
array, since that would be free input. But if the token was "[patient type]",
this would contain values like "elderly" or "hospice"

fields.name: placeholder
fields.description: Placeholder string that will be the default value for the token

Successful responses indicate that Indeed received the job posting. It will be indexed and available (pending spam and fraud detection) at a later time (minutes to hours).

types.name: JobWorkOvertimeSalary
types.description:
An overtime salary expressed as currency amount over a salary period.

This may differ from the base salary and is an extension of JobWorkBaseSalary
with overtime specific properties.

fields.name: period
fields.description:
Pay period to which the pay amount applies.

E.g.: if `period == HOUR`, the following pay amount would be the pay per hour.

fields.name: amount
fields.description:
Pay over the period expressed as a range or an exact amount.

Units are in LOCAL MINOR CURRENCY. Examples:
$102.50 -> 10250
€102.50 -> 10250
£102.50 -> 10250
¥10250  -> 10250

fields.name: isFixedAmount
fields.description:
Is the overtime pay a fixed amount (i.e. a flat rate)?

If true, any overtime worked by employee is paid a fixed amount. For example, if a fixed rate of $1000 for up to 20 hours of overtime work - employees may work 20 hours (or less), and be paid the fixed/flat rate of $1000.
For fixed overtime pay it is also expected that:
`effort.overtimeEffort.amount` specifies the upper bounds of overtime hours paid under the fixed overtime pay scheme (e.g. up to 20 hours overtime / month), and
`effort.overtimeEffort.statutoryEffortForOvertimePay` specifies the minimum hours to be eligible for overtime pay

If false, employer is expected to pay the wage for the overtime work hours based on the overtime pay rate for each hour worked.

The laws governing overtime pay differs from market to market:
JP: https://www.nsasia.co.jp/jsj/jobseeker/knowledge/what-is-fixed-overtime-pay
US: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/17a-overtime

Configuration for executing tasks on Kubernetes clusters.

This configuration specifies how to run your task as a Kubernetes Job,
including which cluster to target and what parameters to pass to your container.

Kubernetes Execution:
- Tasks run as Kubernetes Jobs with configurable resources
- Supports multiple clusters for different environments (dev/staging/prod)
- Parameters become environment variables in your container
- External monitoring through Kubernetes dashboard links

needed for your Kubernetes Job execution.

2. cluster: Optional cluster override (uses default cluster if not specified)
3. parameters: Parameter set for your task execution (optional)

inputFields.name: countryCode
inputFields.description: Country code for which the job is located. Format: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (Example: "CA")

inputFields.name: admin1Code
inputFields.description:
Broadest administrative division under the countryCode.

Examples:
- US - 'WA' (State) or 'PR' (Territory)
- JP - 'JPC' (Region)
- GB - 'ENG' (Country)
- AU - 'QLD' (State) or 'NT' (Territory)

inputFields.name: admin2Code
inputFields.description:
2nd level administrative division under the countryCode.

Examples:
- US - '073' (County)
- JP - 'J13' (Prefecture)
- GB - 'NW' (Region)
- AU - not set

inputFields.name: admin3Code
inputFields.description:
3rd level administrative division under the countryCode.

Examples:
- US - not set
- JP -'J3100174' (District) 'J4271004' (Seirei Shitei Toshi)
- GB - 'MSY' (County)
- AU - not set

inputFields.name: admin4Code
inputFields.description:
4th level administrative division under the countryCode.

Examples:
- US - not set
- JP - 'J4131032' (Ward) 'J4252085' (City)
- GB - not set
- AU - not set

inputFields.name: city
inputFields.description:
Typically represents a city; however, in some markets like Japan may represent a station or district name.

Examples:
- US - 'Bellingham'
- JP - '新宿駅' (Station) '赤坂' (District)
- GB - 'Birkenhead'
- AU - 'Brisbane'

types.name: ManagedInterviewStatus
types.description:
A union representing the various Interview statuses. Each status type corresponds to a specific
state in the interview lifecycle and contains relevant data for that state. To determine the
current status, use the __typename field to identify which union member is active.

Status Types:
- ManagedInterviewRequestedStatus: Interview has been requested by employer
- ManagedInterviewScheduledStatus: Interview has been scheduled by candidate
- ManagedInterviewEmployerCancelledStatus: Interview was cancelled by employer
- ManagedInterviewCandidateCancelledStatus: Interview was cancelled by candidate
- ManagedInterviewCandidateRescheduleRequestedStatus: Candidate requested reschedule (legacy)
- ManagedInterviewCandidateRequestNewTimesStatus: Candidate requested new times

fields.name: jobBasePay
fields.description:
Best recommended base pay component by the salary team. Job base pay can have different pay sources such as employer provided, extracted, inferred that vary in coverage and confidence. The salary team will provide a single job base pay component that contains the best available job base pay data with extraction override applied (we will always use inferred pay as fallback).
Null means pay is not available.

fields.name: jobBasePayInputs
fields.description:
This contains different sources of the base pay that is used to reconcile the jobBasePay. Clients should only access it if jobBasePay does not suit their use case.
Should be nonnull.

fields.name: jobGigPay
fields.description: Gig pay refers to a type of compensation that is not based on traditional time periods such as hourly, daily, or yearly rates. Instead, it is tied to specific tasks or units of work. Examples of gig pay include payment per mile for truck drivers, per class for teachers, or per visit for service providers.

fields.name: jobGigPayInputs
fields.description:
This contains different sources of the gig pay that is used to reconcile the jobGigPay. Clients should only access it if jobGigPay does not suit their use case.
Should be nonnull.

fields.name: jobProjectedPay
fields.description:
Best recommended projected pay to use by the salary team. Projected pay can have different pay sources such as employer-provided,
extracted, estimated that varies in coverage and confidence. The salary team will provide a single job projected pay component that contains the
best available job projected pay data with extraction override applied, and will always use inferred projected pay as fallback.

Unset if projected pay is not available.

fields.name: jobProjectedPayInputs
fields.description:
This contains different sources of the projected pay that is used to reconcile the jobProjectedPay. Clients should only access
if jobProjectedPay does not suit their use case.

This field is always set.

fields.name: jobTaskBasedPay
fields.description: The amount of money one can earn by completing a task that will cost a certain amount of time (taskLengthMinutes).

fields.name: jobTaskBasedPayInputs
fields.description:
This contains different sources of the task-based pay that is used to reconcile the jobTaskBasedPay. Clients should only access it if jobTaskBasedPay does not suit their use case.
Should be nonnull.

fields.name: jobSeekerMarketValue
fields.description:
Annualized market value estimation for job seekers based on resume data.
Excludes behavioral signals.
Always in USD with YEARLY unit of work.

fields.name: jobSeekerMinPayInputs
fields.description:
This contains different components of the JS min pay that is used to reconcile the jobSeekerMinPays.
Clients should only access it if jobSeekerMinPays does not suit their use case.

Each row uses a different model to infer min pay. The model used is indicated by the source field.

fields.name: jobSeekerMinPays
fields.description:
Best recommended JS min pays. It can contain up to one pay per JobSeekerPayUnitOfWork.
Example usage: if you look for yearly min pay, first try to filter on JobSeekerMinPay.pay.unitOfWork == JobSeekerPayUnitOfWork.YEARLY.
    If it yields an empty result, then depending on the use case, try to use the first available pay's payAnnualized if you aim for coverage.

fields.name: bestCountry
fields.description:
Best country that is computed using primary resume.
It will return resume's locale country if locale country has a match with education country, ip country or geo country.
If there is no match, we will return country from the experience section of the resume.
If there is no experience country, we will return the resume locale country (irregardless whether there is a match with other country values)
If there is no resume locale country, we will will return the resume geo country.
If there is no resume geo country, we will return the resume ip country.
Note that this logic is based on UpdogRexAttributes at https://indeed.sourcegraph.com/code.corp.indeed.com/profile-io/updog-rezcommon/-/blob/src/main/java/com/indeed/updog/rezcommon/util/UpdogRezAttributes.java?L30

types.name: MetadataCatalogDataAssetCostAndReach
types.description: Cost and reach metrics for a data asset

fields.name: directCostCategory
fields.description:
Category of average direct cost over the last 30 days (1-5). This value is based on the number of digits (5 stars is $10,000, which is 5 digits) of the cost per month in USD.
< $10 -> 1
< $100 -> 2
< $1,000 -> 3
< $10,000 -> 4
>= $10,000 -> 5

fields.name: indirectCostCategory
fields.description:
Category of average indirect cost over the last 30 days (1-5).
This value is based on the number of digits (5 stars is $10,000, which is 5 digits) of the cost per month in USD for data assets upstream of this one.
For example, if a data asset is built on top of 3 data assets, the average indirect cost will be the average of the 3 data assets.
< $10 -> 1
< $100 -> 2
< $1,000 -> 3
< $10,000 -> 4
>= $10,000 -> 5

fields.name: totalDirectCost
fields.description: Total direct cost over the last 30 days in USD.

fields.name: totalDirectReach
fields.description: Total direct reach, or the number of direct queries, over the last 30 days.

fields.name: totalIndirectCost
fields.description: Total indirect cost over the last 30 days in USD.

fields.name: totalIndirectReach
fields.description: Total indirect reach, or the number of direct queries, over the last 30 days.

fields.name: directReachCategory
fields.description:
Category of average direct reach over the last 30 days (1-5).
This value is based on the number of digits (5 stars is $10,000, which is 5 digits) of the number of queries on the data asset in the last 30 days.
< 10 -> 1
< 100 -> 2
< 1,000 -> 3
< 10,000 -> 4
>= 10,000 -> 5

fields.name: indirectReachCategory
fields.description:
Category of average indirect reach over the last 30 days (1-5).
This value is based on the number of digits (5 stars is $10,000, which is 5 digits) of the number of queries in the last 30 days
on data assets downstream of the data asset.
< 10 -> 1
< 100 -> 2
< 1,000 -> 3
< 10,000 -> 4
>= 10,000 -> 5

types.name: MetadataCatalogDataAssetCostAndReachDetail
types.description: Daily cost and reach metrics for a data asset

fields.name: day
fields.description:
Day in YYYY-MM-DD format. When the granularity is DAY, this will be the day of the cost and reach data.
When the granularity is MONTH, this will be the first day of the month.

fields.name: directReach
fields.description: Count of queries accessing the data asset

fields.name: indirectReach
fields.description: Count of queries accessing data assets downstream of the data asset

fields.name: dailyComputeCost
fields.description: Daily compute cost of the data asset

fields.name: dailyStorageCost
fields.description: Daily storage cost of the data asset

fields.name: indirectDailyComputeCost
fields.description: Daily compute cost for all data assets upstream of the data asset

fields.name: indirectDailyStorageCost
fields.description: Daily storage cost for all data assets upstream of the data asset

fields.name: userCount
fields.description: Count of distinct users accessing the data asset

fields.name: indirectUserCount
fields.description: Count of distinct users accessing data assets downstream of the data asset

inputFields.name: startDate
inputFields.description: Start date for the cost and reach data range, inclusive. This means that the startDate is included in the range.

inputFields.name: endDate
inputFields.description: End date for the cost and reach data range, inclusive. This means that the endDate is included in the range.

inputFields.name: granularity
inputFields.description:
The granularity of the cost and reach data. If the granularity is DAY, the cost and reach will be grouped by day.
If the granularity is MONTH, the cost and reach will be grouped by month. DAY is the default.

enumValues.name: DAY
enumValues.description: Group cost and reach by day. This will take the costs and reach from the startDate to the endDate exclusive.

enumValues.name: MONTH
enumValues.description:
Group cost and reach by month. This will take the costs from the beginning of the month to the end of the month.
If the startDate is not the first day of the month, it will be rounded down to the first day of the month.
If the endDate is not the last day of the month, it will be rounded up to the last day of the month.

- US - not set
- JP -'J3100174' (District) 'J4271004' (Seirei Shitei Toshi)
- GB - 'MSY' (County)
- AU - not set

fields.name: admin4Code
fields.description:
4th level administrative division under the countryCode.

Examples:
- US - not set
- JP - 'J4131032' (Ward) 'J4252085' (City)
- GB - not set
- AU - not set

fields.name: city
fields.description:
Typically represents a city; however, in some markets like Japan may represent a station or district name.

Examples:
- US - 'Bellingham'
- JP - '新宿駅' (Station) '赤坂' (District)

- AU - 'Brisbane'

fields.name: patchEmployer
fields.description:
Creates or updates an employer.

* If Indeed resolves `input.id` to an employer, it updates the specified fields for that employer.

* If Indeed cannot resolve `input.id` to an employer, it creates an employer.

If the request succeeds, the API returns the `employerKey` for the updated or new employer.

Depending on the client type, some Indeed employers are marked as *protected*.

You can update only:

- Non-protected Indeed employers
- Protected Indeed employers created by the same client

You cannot update protected Indeed employers that other clients created.
If you try to do so, the API returns the `FORBIDDEN` error.

When you call the Indeed PLUS APIs, initiate a timeout after 5,000 milliseconds.

Create a new `DraftJobPost` from an existing `EmployerJob`. Given the ID of an `EmployerJob` entity, creates a new `DraftJobPost`
for the purposes of editing and subsequently publishing back to the `EmployerJob` (the job edit flow):
1. The `DraftJobPost` is hydrated with the associated job data from the `EmployerJob`
1. The `DraftJobPost` can be edited and persisted using `patchDraftJobPost`
2. The `DraftJobPost` can be published back to the associated job data of the `EmployerJob`

fields.name: claimEmployerJob
fields.description:
Claims an `EmployerJob` from its ID, producing an updated EmployerJob that points to the claimed job, which will be
populated with data from existing EmployerJob.
This is not guaranteed to succeed; failure scenarios include (but are not limited to):
1. the EmployerJob id is not valid.
2. the EmployerJob is already claimed.
3. in fact the EmployerJob is a hosted job in the first place.
4. the EmployerJob was unclaimed but not enough time has elapsed to make it editable again.

fields.name: submitAppealRejection
fields.description:
Submit the appeal rejection form.

Headers that we need:
- indeed-locale: can use locale query parameter instead (not preferred)
- indeed-co: can use co query parameter instead (not preferred)
- user-agent: can override it by passing the header 'indeed-user-agent'
- indeed-ctk
- indeed-user-ip
Please refer to [OneGraph request headers (consumers)](https://wiki.indeed.com/x/R9M8Gw)

Possible error codes:
- FORBIDDEN (when calling this API without proper auth)
- BAD_USER_INPUT (when the input is invalid)
- INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (when the server encountered an unexpected failure)
- DUPLICATE_ENTRY (when the advertiser has submitted appeal rejection recently)

fields.name: createSourcedJobPostings
fields.description:
Submits a job posting to Indeed.

To submit a job posting, provide details about the job.

The API accepts a complete job posting. If accepted, the API returns an Indeed employer job ID, which is the unique ID for the posting, in the `sourcedPostingId` field. Pending spam and fraud detection, Indeed indexes and makes the job available on Indeed in from minutes to hours.

The API rejects the job posting if it has missing or malformed data, which causes an error at call time. The API returns null in the `sourcedPostingId` field and an error in the standard GraphQL `errors` array.

To update a job posting, provide the same values for the `jobPostingId` and `sourceName` fields and OAuth client ID that you used when you submitted the job posting. You must also provide all required job details even if you are not changing those. The API returns the same unique ID, the Indeed Employer Job ID, that Indeed generated for the submitted job posting.

fields.name: expireSourcedJobsBySourcedPostingId
fields.description:
Expire a posted job using the postingId that was returned from job creation.

Indeed will not verify if the job exists before sending back a response, so the response will always be ACCEPTED.

fields.name: expireSourcedJobsByJobPostingIdAndSource
fields.description:
Expire a posted job using the jobPostingId (referenceId) and the source name.

Indeed will not verify if the job exists before sending back a response, so the response will always be ACCEPTED.

For multi-seat jobs, this can only be used to expire an individual seat by its seatPostingId; it will not expire
an entire multi-seat job by its jobPostingId.

fields.name: scheduleManagedJobseekerInterviewTimeSlot
fields.description:
Schedule a managed jobseeker interview for a given a time slot

Errors:
  INVALID_ARGUMENT any of the input is invalid/out of range
  NOT_FOUND if interview or time slot id do not exist
  CONFLICT if the time slot is not available or the provided updateVersion does not match the current interview version

fields.name: requestNewTimesForJobseekerInterview
fields.description:
Requests new times for a managed interview with given ID. Returns the updated managed interview.

Errors:
  INVALID_ARGUMENT any of the input is invalid/out of range
  NOT_FOUND if interview does not exist
  CONFLICT if there is a conflict when requesting new times
  FAILED_PRECONDITION if the interview is in an invalid state

fields.name: withdrawAccruedTime
fields.description:
Withdraw accrued time, either in the past or in the future
Each accrued time is tied to a worker and location
Withdrawing time subtracts from the worker's accrued time balance

This mutation has some specific errors which are distinguished by the `code` and `subcode` fields within the `extensions` field in the `errors` array:
- {code: FORBIDDEN, subcode: IN_WAITING_PERIOD}: withdrawal is not allowed because worker is in the waiting period, retrying the operation will not result in success
- {code: BAD_USER_INPUT, subcode: INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE}: withdrawal would be larger than available balance
- {code: BAD_USER_INPUT, subcode: ANNUAL_CAP_EXCEEDED}: withdrawal would exceed the annual usage cap
- {code: BAD_USER_INPUT, subcode: INVALID_FIELD_RULE_LOCATION_UUID}: could not resolve a valid `TimeRuleLocation` from rule location uuid, location may have been deleted, uuid could be malformed, etc

fields.name: updateWorkerAccruedTimes

Updates a Worker's Accrued Time Balance. Authorized for SERVICE users 
deltaBalanceMillis will be used to update or initialize the accrued time balance 
millisWorkedSinceLastAccrual will update the field in the accrued time balance

fields.name: cancelAccruedTimes
fields.description:
Cancels pending (but not yet paid) accrued times;
canceling pending accrued time adds back to the worker's accrued time balance

fields.name: markAccruedTimesAsPaid
fields.description:
Marks withdrawn times as paid
These times can no longer be cancelled
Marking accrued time as paid has no effect on the worker's accrued time balance

Authorized for internal SERVICE users

fields.name: unpayAccruedTimes
fields.description:
Unpays accrued times already marked as paid by payrollRunId
The associated pay records cannot be accessed afterwards

Authorized for internal SERVICE users

fields.name: registerTimeWorkers
fields.description:
Register indeed accounts with their associated worker ids in the client's system
i.e. call this operation to register a worker in your system with an indeed account in our system
After registering, users can authenticate with indeed to update time data in our UIs

Note: this operation is effectively an upsert, calling multiple times with the same args safely no-ops

fields.name: setWorkerWorkWeekEnds
fields.description:
Set workers' work week end (WWE) with a worker id + group, given an effective date after which the WWE will be active

 - If the worker has no current WWE, then it will be set to active on the beginning of the WWE
 - If the worker has a current WWE and it matches the input WWE, no new setting will be made
and the worker's current WWE will be return
 - If the worker has a current WWE but there is no overlap, we will create the new WWE anyways
 - If the worker has a current WWE which overlaps AND the current effective date doesn't match the work week start, we will create the new WWE and delete the old WWE

inputFields.name: max
inputFields.description:
The maximum ISO8601 date period or length represented by this range.
This **ONLY** supports the date portion of ISO8601 durations.

If the range is open, exclude this field or set it to `null`.
If the there is no range, but a single period, use
the same value as `min`.
