fields.name: create
fields.description:
Creates a new Pay-Per-Hire contract for an EmployerJob.

This method automatically creates an underlying ads campaign.

fields.name: pause
fields.description:
Pauses the active contract by the provided EmployerJob ID.

This operation is idempotent, i.e., pausing an already paused contract will result in success.

fields.name: resume
fields.description:
Resumes the paused contract by the provided EmployerJob ID.

This operation is idempotent, i.e., resuming an already active contract will result in success.

fields.name: close
fields.description:
Closes the active contract by the provided EmployerJob ID.

This operation is idempotent, i.e., closing an already closed contract will result in success.

fields.name: closeByAdvertiser
fields.description:
Closes the active contract by the provided EmployerJob ID.

This operation is idempotent, i.e., closing an already closed contract will result in success.
This operation will succeed even if the job doesn't have any PPH contracts associated with it. In this case, the operation will return null as a contract.

fields.name: updateLatestContract
fields.description:
Updates the latest contract for the provided EmployerJob ID.

This operation is idempotent, i.e., updating an already updated contract will result in success.
If the job doesn't have any PPH contracts associated with it, the operation will return JOB_HAS_NO_ACTIVE_PPH_CONTRACT error.

types.name: PreApplyCandidate
types.description:
A Candidate that has interacted with a given job but has not yet applied.
Pre-apply candidates are unique at a job level--this means that if the same jobseeker interacts with two different jobs of the same advertiser, two separate pre-apply candidate entities will exist. However, if the same jobseeker interacts multiple times with the same job, only one PreApplyCandidate entity will exist.

fields.description:

Note: it will be globally unique for predefined questions

fields.description:
Question type
textarea
text
select
hierarchical
multiselect
date
file
information
pagebreak

fields.description:
Apply question category
Screener - screener questions
Demographic - demographic questions

i.e. How many years of Customer Service experience do you have?

fields.name: text
fields.description: Informational text

fields.name: format
fields.description:
The accepted format of the input. If used with type:text, the question will accept only integer, decimal,
or numeric_text validation answers. If used with type:date, the question will only accept SimpleDateFormat with MM.
This is required Yes for type=date No for type=text

Text formats:
integer
decimal
numeric_text
other locale specific formats (please use Unicode CLDR as a guide)
Date formats:
integer
dd/MM/yyyy

fields.name: required
fields.description:
Identifies a question as required, default is false.
When required:true is present, Indeed Apply forces a non-empty text field or a non-empty selection.
When the required parameter is not present, questions are optional.
If a question is optional, a possible answer value is "".

fields.name: hardRequired
fields.description:
Whether this value represents a hard requirement (dealbreaker) or not. If null, the value is
unspecified. This value should always be present for multi-select input values associated with an
ALL_OF requirement. In all other cases, this value should be absent.

fields.name: limit
fields.description: For type=text and type=textarea, the character limit for the answer.

fields.name: min
fields.description:
For format=integer or format=decimal, the minimum value for the answer. For type=date, the date that the answer
must be on or after.

fields.name: max
fields.description:
For format=integer or format=decimal the maximum value for the answer. For type=date, the date the answer must
be on or before.

fields.name: sanitize
fields.description:
Sanitize/delete answer set mutation
This operation removes answer sets for specified entities using their entityIds. Key features:

Idempotent design: Multiple executions or retries yield the same end result.
Consistent outcome: The final state remains unchanged regardless of the number of operations performed.
Metadata feedback: The response includes a delete count, indicating the number of answer sets removed during the operation.
This API ensures reliable and predictable answer set deletion while providing useful metadata about the process.

The deletion could end up with 4 scenarios:
     * Case 1 : Full deletion success.
       This will be input_size == deletedCount, with no error.
     * Case 2 : Full deletion success with some files not in database.
       This will be count < input_size, without error.
     * Case 3: Complete failure. This will be zero count and error out completely to throw exception.
       This will be count == 0, and error.
     * Case 4: Partial failure. This will be count < input_suze, and with partial error.
       This will be count < input_size, and error as the operation stopped before completion of all records. Client

       If after retry the operation is still failing, the client should contact the team for support.

fields.name: myJobsApplies
fields.description:
Retrieve applies and their additional metadata made by a job seeker identified by CTK and account ID on a job board identified by client name.
This query conforms to [GraphQL Cursor Connections Specification](https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm).

## HTTP Headers
- `indeed-ctk`: Applies that match the provided CTK will be returned.
- `indeed-fed-account-id`: Applies that match the provided account ID will be returned. When both CTK and account id are present a union of both sets of applies will be returned.
- `indeed-fed-client-name`: Client name should identify a job board. Only applies made on the specified job board will be returned.

## Parameters
- `input`: Includes filter parameters. Please see `MyJobsAppliesInput` definition for details.
- **Pagination parameters**: Please refer to [GraphQL Cursor Connections Specification](https://relay.dev/graphql/connections.htm) for the pagination behavior.
    - `first`: Should be less than or equal to 50. If a number greater than 50 is given, it will be treated as 50 without errors.
    - `after`
    - `last`: Should be less than or equal to 50. If a number greater than 50 is given, it will be treated as 50 without errors.
    - `before`

## Response
A list of `MyJobsApply` matching with `input` made by a job seeker on a job board wrapped in `MyJobsAppliesConnection` structure.

fields.name: getAllAutoInvites
fields.description:
Retrieves all AutoInvite configurations based on the advertiser of the user making the request.

Pagination behavior with reasonable defaults:
- **Default**: When no parameters provided → returns first 20 items
- **Forward pagination**: Use 'first' + 'after' → get next N items after cursor
- **Backward pagination**: Use 'last' + 'before' → get previous N items before cursor
- **Validation**: Cannot combine forward (first/after) with backward (last/before) parameters

Examples:
- `getAllAutoInvites` → first 20 items
- `getAllAutoInvites(first: 10)` → first 10 items  
- `getAllAutoInvites(first: 10, after: "cursor123")` → next 10 items after cursor
- `getAllAutoInvites(last: 5)` → last 5 items

args.name: first
args.description: Forward pagination: number of items to return (default: 20). Cannot be used with 'last'.

args.name: after
args.description: Forward pagination: cursor to start after. Cannot be used with 'before'.

args.name: last
args.description: Backward pagination: number of items from end. Cannot be used with 'first'.

args.name: before
args.description: Backward pagination: cursor to end before. Cannot be used with 'after'.

fields.name: brsOutcomePredictions
fields.description:
Given a budget, **predict** the outcomes for one or more jobs.

Depending on the product type provided in the input, the outcomes could be:

- Sponsored Jobs

   - Clicks
   - Apply starts
   - Applies
- IHP Events

   - Interview RSVPs
   - Interview shows

Supported job types:

- Live job: An existing job at Indeed. JobKey (Default) or AggJobId must be provided.
- Prospective job: A hypothetical job (Title, location, country and language must be provided)

Supported products:

- Sponsored jobs
- IHP events

fields.name: brsBudgetRecommendations
fields.description:
Given a target outcome for some jobs, **recommend** a budget to achieve that target.

Depending on the product type provided in the input, the target outcomes could be:

- Sponsored Jobs

   - Clicks
   - Apply starts
   - Applies
- IHP Events

   - Interview RSVPs
   - Interview shows

Supported job types:

- Live job: An existing job at Indeed. JobKey (Default) or AggJobId must be provided.
- Prospective job: A hypothetical job (Title, location, country and language must be provided)

Supported products:

- Sponsored jobs
- IHP events

fields.name: brsCampaignBudgetDistribution
fields.description:
Given a campaign total budget, and the campaign's list of jobs along with their constraints and goals, distribute
the campaign budget on the jobs efficiently while respecting the constraints and maximizing the goals of each job.

Supported job types:

- Live job: An existing job at Indeed. JobKey (Default) or AggJobId must be provided.

Supported products:

- Sponsored jobs

Backward pagination -

Bidirectional pagination is not supported.

fields.name: findHireApplications
fields.description:
Query for hire applications with filter and pagination.

Pagination:

We use cursor based pagination but instead of storing id's we are using indexes.
If only `first` is provided this query will return the first N count of elements.
The last element index returned will be included in the `pageInfo` result variable, `endCursor`.
`endCursor` can then be supplied to the `after` variable in order to fetch the next N count results starting after that index.
Backwards pagination is also available with the `last` and `before` variables;
Only two pagination variables are supported for one query.

Forward Pagination: (`first`), (`first`, `after`)

Backwards Pagination: (`last`), (`last`, `before`)

args.name: filter
args.description: Filter for hire applications

args.name: first
args.description: For forward pagination. Max: 1000

args.name: after
args.description: The index to retrieve after.  If this was "10" you will receive results starting at index 11

args.name: last
args.description: For backward pagination. Max: 1000

args.name: before
args.description: The index to retrieve before.  e.g. Find `last` count of applications before index "10"

fields.name: jobData
fields.description:
Retrieve job data for input jobKeys. If a jobKey is not found no data is returned

_HTTP Headers:_

- **indeed-ctk** : User CTK used for personalization.
- **indeed-prforce-groups** : Used to force proctor groups for JobRetrievalService and JobSearchService requests. Format: [Forcing Groups](https://opensource.indeedeng.io/proctor/docs/using-groups/#forcing-groups)
- **indeed-fed-client-roles** : Used to present the roles of the client. This is a multi-value header. Currently, the following roles are supported:
  - _**allow-glassdoor-data**_ - Allow the client to access Glassdoor filters, facets in jobSearch and glassdoor field in jobData.
  - _**allow-nowhere-jobs**_ - Allow the client to include nowhere jobs in the results. This role is the prerequisite for getting nowhere jobs in the jobData query.
  - _**allow-fraudulent-jobs**_ - Allow the client to include jobs that are confirmed fraudulent in the results. This role is the prerequisite for getting `isConfirmedFraudulent` field in the `Job`.
  - _**allow-nowhere-jobs-as-organic**_ - Allow the client to include nowhere jobs in the job search results. This role is the prerequisite for getting nowhere jobs in the jobSearch query.
  - _**allow-recruit-data**_ - Allow the client to access recruit-specific fields (e.g. attributesBlob) in jobData.


_URL Parameters:_

- **locale** : Used for localizing response data. Format: [BCP 47 language tag](https://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47) (Example: "en-US")

args.name: jobKeys
args.description:
This field is deprecated in favor of `input` - however, if `jobKeys` is set,
requests must include at least 1 jobKey and are limited to a maximum of 1200 jobKeys.  Maximum of 500 unique `jobKeys` are allowed.

If `jobs` is set, requests must include at least one `JobDataKeyInput` and are limited to a maximum of
1200 `JobDataKeyInput`.  Maximum of 500 unique `jobKeys` are allowed.

Also, only one of 'jobKeys' or 'input' can be specified in the query - not both.

fields.name: jobSearch
fields.description:
Search for jobs

_Count Only Requests:_
To execute "count" only request, either specify a `limit` of 0 or do not request the `JobSearchPayload.results`

_HTTP Headers:_

- **indeed-ctk** : Used for personalizing search results (e.g., ranking and matching)
 - **indeed-co** : Target country for search. Format: 2-letter country code validated against a [pre-defined list of supported Indeed sites](https://wiki.indeed.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=456971079) (Example: "JP")
- **indeed-locale** : Used for localizing response data. Format: [BCP 47 language tag](https://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47). Language portion can influence search matching (Example: "en-US")
- **indeed-prforce-groups** : Used to force proctor groups for JobRetrievalService and JobSearchService requests. Format: [Forcing Groups](https://opensource.indeedeng.io/proctor/docs/using-groups/#forcing-groups)
- **indeed-fed-client-roles** : Used to present the roles of the client. This is a multi-value header. Currently, the following roles are supported:
  - _**allow-sponsored-jobs**_ - Allow the client to include sponsored jobs in the results. This role is the prerequisite for using the 'includeSponsoredResults' field in the jobSearch query.
  - _**allow-glassdoor-data**_ - Allow the client to access Glassdoor filters, facets in jobSearch and glassdoor field in jobData.
- **indeed-fed-client-flags** : Used for enabling client-specific behavior. This is a multi-value header. Currently, the following flags are supported:
  - _**return-sponsored-jobs-as-organic**_ - Handle sponsored jobs as if they are organic. Any sponsored-specific logic such as auction is skipped. The 'allow-sponsored-jobs' client role is ignored.

args.name: what
args.description:
Search query

Note that any composition of search filters should be done with the filters input and not stuffed in the what.

**Examples:**
- "nurse"
- "part-time"

args.name: searchCriteria
args.description: A serialized representation of the job search

args.name: location
args.description:
Search location

Can not provide a non-empty where and provide any JobSearchKeywordFilterInput on `location.key` field (a.k.a multi-location search) at the same time. Otherwise a BadUserInputException will be thrown

args.name: cursor
args.description:
Allow clients to page through results. Leave unset for first page results

To page forward set cursor to JobSearchPayload pageInfo.nextCursor
To page back set cursor to JobSearchPayload pageInfo.prevCursor
To page forward or backward more than one page, use cursor in JobSearchPayload pageInfo.nextPages or pageInfo.prevPages

args.name: limit
args.description:
Maximum number of results to be returned. Must be at least 1 and at most 100

A request fails if this field is modified during pagination, that is, this field does not match the limit in a valid "cursor"

The value for `limit` is ignored when `JobSearchPayload.results` field is not requested; defaults to 10 otherwise

args.name: numPrevPages
args.description: Maximum number of pages to be returned in `JobSearchPayloadPageInfo` for previous pages (`prevPages`). Must be at least 1 and at most 5

args.name: numNextPages
args.description: Maximum number of pages to be returned in `JobSearchPayloadPageInfo` for next pages (`nextPages`). Must be at least 1 and at most 5

args.name: sort
args.description: Order to sort search results

args.name: lastSearchTime
args.description:
Time of last search in milliseconds. This is used to determine `sinceLastSearchCount` in `JobSearchPayload`.
This parameter does not affect the age of jobs returned in results.

args.name: filters
args.description: Specify filters to narrow down search results

args.name: includeSponsoredResults
args.description:
Include sponsored results or not in the results. Do not return any sponsored job if this field is not specified.

**Note:** In order to include sponsored jobs, clients need to apply for the access to this field.
Please refer to this [wiki](https://wiki.indeed.com/pages/viewpage.action?spaceKey=JSAPI&title=Jobseeker+GraphQL+API+Documentation#JobseekerGraphQLAPIDocumentation-HowdoIgetaccesstosponsoredjobcontentviathejobSearchAPI?)
to get the permission.

If the client does not have the access permission, no sponsored job is returned regardless of what value is
specified for this field. In addition, if 'return-sponsored-jobs-as-organic' client flag is specified,
this field is ignored.

args.name: origin
args.description:
Controls whether the search results should be counted as impressions.  For any search triggered by a JobSeeker action this
should either be omitted or set to USER_INPUT and the results will be counted as impressions.  If the search is triggered
by something that is not directly by a JobSeeker action, for example providing additional recommendations this should be
set to GENERATED and the results will not be counted as impressions.

If this field is not set, it will default to USER_INPUT.

args.name: placementId
args.description: Placement id for defining the job impression surface of this query. Indeed+ clients require this parameter to be provided, and the validity will be checked internally.

args.name: pageTrackingKey
args.description:
A client created tracking key used to link all interactions from the same page together.
Must only contain alphanumeric [A-Za-z0-9] and dashes
Must be between 12 - 40 characters in size
Must be unique, it is recommended to use an UUID or something equivalent (non-human readable).

types.name: RcpOutreachIneligibilityReasonInput
types.description:
Specific reason why an employer might be ineligible to reach out to a recommended candidate

After Project Galaxy Phase 1 Monetization, an employer with a FTP/PPC job will become outreach ineligible if they:

- Used up their trial subscription (14 days & 20 invites).
- Used up their invites as part of their standard/pro subscription (they can also choose to purchase more invites).

If we don't change outreach ineligibility reasons right now, we would see that an employer is outreach ineligible due to their job posting type (FTP or PPC) even though it is due to their subscription type.

TODO: Change the outreach ineligibility reasons to reflect that it is due to an employer not having the proper Resume Search subscription, instead of the job being FTP or PPC.

enumValues.name: JOB_LIM
enumValues.description: The job has hit its lifetime limit of 200 invites

enumValues.name: FTP_JOB
enumValues.description:
The job is a "Free to Post" job, which means the employer can view candidates, but is not allowed to invite them

inputFields.description: ID of previous interview session to use as input source

inputFields.name: useBestEffort
inputFields.description:
When useBestEffort is true, the default validation behavior is not applied, and
invalid or incomplete data will not be copied into the draft, but also does not raise an exception.

Any validation failure on lower level fields will result in the entire top level field being null.

The only exception to this rule is jobs - invalid/missing jobs will be excluded from the draft, but
valid jobs will still be added to the draft.

For example, a missing address for an in-person interview method will result in a null "method" section of the
draft, which must be populated by update before the event can be published.

Fields which were skipped during duplication due to a validation error, if useBestEffort was set to true

For "jobs" only, this only means at least one job was not copied.
For all other fields, the entire top level input was skipped.

types.name: ResourceAvailabilitySettings
types.description:
Availability settings for a [Calendar].

The availability settings specify the times when a calendar is available to schedule
events. The actual calendar availability is calculated with these steps:

1. The default state for a particular time is unavailable
2. Add time periods that match the [include] settings
3. Remove time periods that match [exclude] settings
4. Remove time periods that are not in the availability [window]
5. Remove any events scheduled on the calendar
6. Remove any holds registered on the calendar

The remaining time periods determine when the calendar is available.

fields.name: include
fields.description: Settings that specify time the calendar is potentially available.

fields.name: exclude
fields.description: Settings that specify time the calendar is explicitly unavailable.

fields.name: window
fields.description: Window in the future that events can be scheduled on the calendar.

fields.name: timezone
fields.description: Time zone to interpret the availability rules with.

types.name: RunTaskInput
types.description:
Complete configuration for submitting a new task for execution.

You can run a task in two ways (provide either k8sTaskConfig OR assetId):

1. **Direct Configuration**: Provide k8sTaskConfig with explicit task configuration
2. **Asset-Based**: Provide assetId to run a pre-configured asset with optional overrides

Retry Strategy:
- Provide retryStrategy to specify retry count and timeout configurations
- If not specified: defaults to standard retry strategy (1 retry, PT24H timeouts) for direct config, uses asset's retry strategy for assets

inputFields.name: retryStrategy
inputFields.description: Retry strategy configuration. If not specified: defaults to standard strategy for direct config, uses asset's strategy for assets.

inputFields.name: parameters
inputFields.description: Optional parameters to override asset defaults (only used when assetId is provided)

inputFields.name: cluster
inputFields.description: Optional cluster override (only used when assetId is provided)

inputFields.name: suppressDownstreams
inputFields.description: Optional flag to suppress downstream tasks (only used when assetId is provided). Defaults to false.

types.name: SchedulingWindow
types.description:
Configuration for calculating time windows in scheduled tasks.

This object defines how to calculate the time window for a trigger:
- duration: The size of the window (e.g., "P1D" for 1 day, "PT2H" for 2 hours)
- offset: How far back to go before calculating the window backwards (e.g., "PT1H" for 1 hour offset)

Example: For a daily window with 1 hour offset:
- duration: "P1D" (1 day window)  
- offset: "PT1H" (start 1 hour ago)

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Window size using ISO 8601 duration format (e.g., 'P1D' for 1 day, 'PT2H' for 2 hours)

fields.name: offset
fields.description: Offset backwards from current time using ISO 8601 duration format (e.g., 'PT1H' for 1 hour)

fields.name: createConversation
fields.description:
This call must be initiated to retrieve a conversationId for Scout.

The returned ScoutConversation.id is an IRI-encoded conversation identifier that should be used
in subsequent operations (like postChatMessage). 

Important UUID vs IRI distinction:
- The input sessionUuid (if provided) is a raw UUID
- The returned conversation.id is an IRI-encoded version of that UUID
- Always use conversation.id (not the raw sessionUuid) for subsequent operations

Usage:
- Pass the returned conversation.id to postChatMessage as the conversationId
- Store the conversation.id for conversation management and message history retrieval
- Do NOT use the raw sessionUuid input for subsequent operations

inputFields.description: Answer value for the screener question

inputFields.name: textarea
inputFields.description: A question that requires a long-form answer. Appears as a multi-line text entry field.

inputFields.name: text
inputFields.description:
A question that requires a short answer. Appears as a single-line text entry field.

For more information on the available formats for text questions, see the following examples and the [JSON questions parameters](https://docs.indeed.com/indeed-apply/screener-questions#json-questions-parameters). The formats are `integer`, `decimal`, and `numeric_text`.

inputFields.name: select
inputFields.description:
A question that has multiple-choice answers. Appears as a select menu that enables the applicant to select a single answer.

If you include from one to five answers, each answer appears with a radio button. If you include more than five answers, they appear in a dropdown list.

inputFields.name: multiselect
inputFields.description: A question that has multiple answers. Appears as a list of checkboxes that enables the applicant to select multiple answers.

inputFields.name: hierarchical
inputFields.description:
A question that shows additional questions and answers based on previously selected answers. For example, you might ask an applicant to choose a state. After they choose a state, you can show a dropdown list of cities within that state. Each hierarchy of questions is limited to three levels. For example: state, city, and county.

A hierarchy of questions are similar to conditional questions. However, a hierarchy of questions are better suited to question types where an initial selection defines potential answers to subsequent questions. Using the hierarchy functionality reduces the number of questions needed to get related information.

inputFields.name: date
inputFields.description:
A question that has a date as an answer. Appears as a text field that accepts a date.

This screener question type requires either the dd/MM/yyyy format or a locale-specific format that meets Unicode CLDR formatting.

Indeed uses the `SimpleDateFormat`. You must format the month as MM. Using mm results in misconfiguration.

The format of `type=date` impacts how the application is passed to the ATS and how the minimum and maximum values are parses. The job seeker still enters the date based on their locale, not the specified format, and validation error messages are in their locale’s format. To prevent confusion, use yyyy instead of yy in the format.

inputFields.name: file
inputFields.description:
A question that requires a file upload as an answer, such as certifications, portfolios, or example work. Appears as a file upload interface. The answer returned in the JSON `POST` request contains these fields: `contentType`, `data`, and `fileName`.

Valid files types are:
doc
docx
gif
jfif
jif
jpe
jpeg
jpg
pdf
png
rtf
tif
tiff
txt

inputFields.name: information
inputFields.description:
A text display that does not require a response. Appears as explanatory text or section headings.
For details, see [information](https://docs.indeed.com/indeed-apply/screener-questions#information).

inputFields.name: pageBreak
inputFields.description: Groups questions on a page. Questions defined between two pagebreak types appear on the same page. You can group up to 20 questions on a page. By default, Indeed shows three questions on a page on desktop and groups all questions on a page for mobile.

inputFields.description:
ID of the created conversation event, it also serves as an idempotency key.
Clients should generate this unique eventId if they cannot ensure a message is sent at most once.

For instance, if an 'interview request' event triggers this request, the event's identifier should be integrated into the key.
It's crucial that the same source can reproduce this key consistently.

types.name: SourcedJobPosting
types.description:
Return type for an accepted job posting. Indeed considers a job as accepted if it is a complete job that is accepted for indexing.

Even if accepted, it might not appear on Indeed if it does not adhere to the Indeed [Job Posting Standards](https://indeedinc.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/115005915763).

If an accepted job does not appear on Indeed, see [My job is not shown on Indeed](https://indeedinc.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/115005915763).

fields.name: sourcedPostingId
fields.description:
UUID for the job, or the Indeed Employer Job ID.

Indeed generates this unique ID for each submitted job posting.

Use this ID to expire the job posting.

fields.name: employerJobId
fields.description:
The EmployerJob entity ID associated with the sourced job posting.

This entity ID is equivalent to a sourcedPostingId, but it is in the base-64 encoded Indeed Resource Identifier format.

Thus, this entity ID can be used to query the posting as an EmployerJob via the node & nodes queries.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingApplyMethodInput
types.description: Input object with information about how to apply to the job.

inputFields.name: indeedApply
inputFields.description: Apply through Indeed Apply.

inputFields.name: title
inputFields.description: Job title. Do not include other types of information, such as employment type, job location, job descriptions, copies, or headlines.

inputFields.name: subtitle
inputFields.description:
Subheader for the job title.

**Example**: "A bright and pleasant workplace"

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description:
Description for the job posting.

This field is limited to 65000 bytes. ASCII characters are 1 byte, while other characters are from 2 to 3 bytes.

Ensure that the information in this field matches the details on the URL in your `SourcedJobPostingMetadataInput.url` field.

This field is the source of the raw text that Indeed shows to job seekers. Includes all job-relevant information, including text that can also be provided in other fields in the XML, such as education or experience.

**Note:** Job descriptions require HTML formatting. For a list of supported HTML elements, see [Enterprise ATS Integration with Indeed: Formatting guidelines](https://developer.indeed.com/docs/indeed-apply/enterprise-ats/#formatting_guidelines).

inputFields.name: descriptionFormatting
inputFields.description:
How to parse description.

You can use an HTML-formatted job description by passing `RICH_FORMATTING`. In the HTML job description, there are
additional constraints on the HTML attributes and element order.

inputFields.name: salary
inputFields.description: Structured salary information for this job.

inputFields.name: hasProbationaryPeriod
inputFields.description: Indicates whether the job has a probationary period.

inputFields.name: probationaryPeriod
inputFields.description:
Probationary period with a specific salary.

In Japan, some jobs have probationary periods with different salaries. Use this entity only for jobs in Japan with a probationary period. If your job is not in Japan or is in Japan and does not have a probationary period, do not include this entity. It might lead to your job being moderated.

inputFields.name: location
inputFields.description:
Job location.

If creating a job with `seats`, specify the country of all seats ONLY.

For jobs with multiple seats in multiple locations, all locations MUST be in the same country.

inputFields.name: benefits
inputFields.description:
A list of benefits associated with the job.

Specify separate, distinct benefits as multiple strings in the list.

If the job does not have explicit non-salary benefits, specify an empty list.

inputFields.name: seats
inputFields.description:
For modeling shifts on an individual or repeated basis, a seat must be defined
with this information. Each seat represents one hiring need. Each seat represents a single
job posting on indeed.com. At this time, the Job Sync API only accepts up to one seat, which
maintains the contract of a 1:1 relationship between `CreateSourcedJobPostingsInput` and
job posts in downstream systems.

A single sourced job posting must have a maximum of 100 seats.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingBreakDurationInput
types.description: The duration for a break without a set time during the shift.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingBreakTimePeriodInput
types.description:
Breaks may be defined as either a fixed time range during a shift, or a fixed duration.

In cases where workers are given a break, but it could occur any time during the shift,
only a `timeDuration` should be defined. If the break has a set and unchanging time during a shift,
specify a `timeRange`.

Exactly one of the two must be defined.

inputFields.name: timeRange
inputFields.description: For defining a specific set time a break will occur.

inputFields.name: timeDuration
inputFields.description:
For defining only the duration of a break, which may occur at an undefined time during a shift,
such as when a 'rush' at food service or retail slows down.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingExtractedAttributesInput
types.description: Input object with information about automatically extracted taxonomy attributes

inputFields.name: employerAcceptedAttributes
inputFields.description: One or more SUIDs or strings that represent taxonomy attributes that were automatically extracted and accepted by the employer.

inputFields.name: employerRejectedAttributes
inputFields.description: One or more SUIDs or strings that represent taxonomy attributes that were automatically extracted and rejected by the employer.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingFineGrainedJobSalaryInput
types.description:
Input object with salary information for the job.

Use minor currency units, such as cents, pence, or yen, for salary values.

inputFields.name: salaryPeriod
inputFields.description:
The period that applies to other fields in this input object.

For example, if `salaryPeriod == MONTHLY`, then working hours are the expected number of working hours per month.

To ensure your job shows on Indeed, one of the following values is recommended.

* `DAY`
* `HOUR`
* `MILE`
* `MONTH`
* `WEEK`
* `YEAR`

inputFields.name: totalSalaryMinor
inputFields.description:
The total salary of a job for the specified period, in minor currency units.

**Examples**:

`$102.50 -> 10250`

`€102.50 -> 10250`

`£102.50 -> 10250`

`¥10250 -> 10250`

inputFields.name: workingHours
inputFields.description:
Expected number of hours of work expected per period. This is not necessarily a maximum number of hours a worker can
work during the `period`, but an expected minimum.

Examples:

- if `period` is `HOUR` and `totalSalaryMinor` is the amount of wage per hour, then this field should be set to 1.
- if `period` is `MONTH`, then this field should be set to the total working hours per month.

inputFields.name: totalOvertimeHours
inputFields.description: Total maximum overtime work hours for this job in the specified period, through `period`.

inputFields.name: statutoryOvertimeHours
inputFields.description:
Statutory overtime work hours in the specified period, through `period`.

Accepts fractions of an hour.

inputFields.name: fixedOvertimeSalaryMinor
inputFields.description:
If the overtime pay, `fixedOvertimePay`, is not included in the pay and is a fixed value, specify it in this field.

**Examples**:

`$102.50 -> 10250`

`€102.50 -> 10250`

`£102.50 -> 10250`

`¥10250 -> 10250`

inputFields.name: fixedOvertimePay
inputFields.description:
If a base salary already presumes a certain number of overtime hours without pay, a job must positively affirm this in this field.

**Example**: In the US, jobs that meet certain requirements can be designated as _overtime exempt_.

For more information, see the [US Department of Labor website](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/17a-overtime).

**Example**: In Japan, fixed overtime means that the overtime wage is already fixed into the salary. For details, see [pay](https://www.nsasia.co.jp/jsj/jobseeker/knowledge/what-is-fixed-overtime-pay).

types.name: SourcedJobPostingFormattingType
types.description: Types for formatting.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingIndeedApplyInput
types.description:
Input object of Indeed Apply information for the job.

<!--
The following indeed-apply parameters are gathered from other parts of the schema:
indeed-apply-jobUrl - (JobMetadataInput.postUrl) The canonical URL to the complete job description.
indeed-apply-jobId - (JobMetadataInput.jobPostingId) The ID of the job, used for your own internal tracking.
indeed-apply-jobCompanyName - (JobSourceInput.companyName) The name of the company. If you do not include a companyName, we derive this from other information in JobSourceInput.
indeed-apply-jobLocation - (PendingJob.location - repeated) The location of the job.
indeed-apply-jobTitle - (JobBodyInput.title) The title of the job to display externally.
-->

inputFields.name: jobMeta
inputFields.description:
Additional information.

This information is not displayed externally, but it is sent when using the apply through the `POST` URL.

inputFields.name: postUrl
inputFields.description: URL to which Indeed posts the application data. Encode this URL. Must be HTTPS.

inputFields.name: phoneRequired
inputFields.description:
Indicates whether the phone number field is displayed on the job.

Default is `OPTIONAL`.

inputFields.name: coverLetterRequired
inputFields.description:
Indicates whether the message or cover letter field is required.

Default is `OPTIONAL`.

inputFields.name: resumeRequired
inputFields.description:
Indicates whether a resume is required (`YES`) or optional (`OPTIONAL`), or whether to hide the resume upload option from the user (`NO`).

If you specify optional or hidden (`NO`), you must include screener questions. You must support .pdf, .doc, .docx, .rtf, and .txt formats for resumes.

Default is `YES`.

inputFields.name: resumeFieldsRequired
inputFields.description:
List of resume fields that the job seeker's resume must include.

This field overwrites the phone configuration parameters, if provided.

inputFields.name: resumeFieldsOptional
inputFields.description:
List of resume fields that the job seeker's resume can include.

This field overwrites the phone configuration parameters, if provided.

inputFields.name: nameFormat
inputFields.description: Indicates whether a single field for the full name is sufficient in the apply form, or the full name must be split into first and last name.

inputFields.name: applyQuestions
inputFields.description: URL that returns a JSON-formatted string of questions to ask during the Indeed Apply application process.

inputFields.name: applyQuestionsDetails
inputFields.description: Screener questions schema for Indeed Apply application process

inputFields.name: apiToken
inputFields.description: API token. Required for Indeed Apply. Refer to your [Partner Console account](https://console.indeed.com/integrations/home) to view the assigned Indeed Apply API Token credentials.

inputFields.name: finishApplicationUrl
inputFields.description:
A URL that the job seeker is prompted to visit after applying
by clicking Continue on the application confirmation page.

URLs should be properly encoded. Consider the following:
- https://example.com/indeed_finish_application/?indeed_apply_id={indeed_apply_id}
    - {indeed_apply_id} indicates that known field's value - the encrypted `indeed_apply_id` - will
      be inserted into the URL. When Indeed calls the URL, it would look like
      `https://example.com/indeed_finish_application/?indeed_apply_id=6339da3ba0f6f723851334e86a0f7c34cf00f51078cc770b0cace3277f6b99df`
- When making requests to the Job Sync API, the URL must be encoded. The above example is not
  a valid `WebUrl`
    - Correct: `https://example.com/indeed_finish_application/?indeed_apply_id=%7Bindeed_apply_id%7D`

Do not use the this field without approval from Indeed.

inputFields.name: withdrawHookUrl
inputFields.description:
Canonical URL to the API endpoint that is called inform ATS withdraw action has been processed

For jobs onboarded to Indeed's candidate withdrawal system.

inputFields.name: withdrawExpirationAt
inputFields.description:
The point in time when a job seeker can no longer withdraw an application from a job.

For jobs onboarded to Indeed's candidate withdrawal system.

inputFields.name: contactEmail
inputFields.description:
Email address of the contact for the job.

Required by the Indeed Search Quality team.

Indeed recommends that the contact email domain be the same email domain as the URL of the company, or the `companyWebsite`.

inputFields.name: contactName
inputFields.description: Name for the client's contact.

inputFields.name: contactPhone
inputFields.description: Phone number for the client's contact.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingJobContactInput
types.description:
Input object that lists job contacts.

Provides users access to the job in some systems on Indeed.

inputFields.name: contactType
inputFields.description:
Closest roles that the contact has:

* `contact`. For the primary contact information for the job.
* `hiring manager`. For the hiring manager.
* `recruiter`. For a recruiter.
* `user`. For other users, such as interviewers or coordinators.
* Both `contact` and `recruiter`. If the contact for a job is also the recruiter, for instance.

inputFields.name: contactInfo
inputFields.description: Information about how to reach the contact.

inputFields.name: companyName
inputFields.description: Name of the company where the job is performed.

inputFields.name: companyWebsite
inputFields.description: Root website of the company. For example, `https://www.indeed.com`. If the company is a franchise, use the brand website.

inputFields.name: sourceName
inputFields.description:
The name of the parent organization that is hiring for the role. For example, if subsidiaries or franchises with multiple-branded locations under the same company exist, those jobs have the same value in the `sourceName` field. The `sourceName` must be unique across all job groups, and a `sourceName` can have only one `sourceType`, which is the type of organization.

When a user claims their jobs on Indeed, this identifier determines the granular group of jobs that are associated with their account.

inputFields.name: sourceType
inputFields.description:
Type of organization that is hiring for this role:

* `Employer`. Direct employer, ad agency acting on behalf of the direct employer, or recruitment process outsourcer (RPO).
* `Job Board`. Job board.
* `Staffing Agency`. Staffing agency or recruitment firm.

inputFields.name: externalEmployerId
inputFields.description: Deprecated. Use `employerIds` instead.
inputFields.deprecationReason: this field will be deprecated together with employerKey, use employerIds instead.

inputFields.name: employerKey
inputFields.description: Deprecated. Use `employerIds` instead.
inputFields.deprecationReason: this field will be deprecated together with externalEmployerId, use employerIds instead.

inputFields.name: employerIds
inputFields.description: Replaces `externalEmployerId` and `employerKey`.

inputFields.name: isPlacement
inputFields.description:
Is a job for placement business.

* If true, field `sourceType` must be `Staffing Agency`
* Default is false.

inputFields.name: originFeedSystemName
inputFields.description:
The name or identifier of the system where the job originated.
Used for distinguishing between systems where one partner brings jobs from multiple origin systems.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingLocationInput
types.description: Implementation detail: We'll need to format this info into the existing detailed_location UDDT.

inputFields.name: latitude
inputFields.description: Latitude of the location where the job is performed.

inputFields.name: longitude
inputFields.description: Longitude of the location where the job is performed.

inputFields.name: country
inputFields.description:
Country code of the country where this job is located. For the list of country codes, see [Supported language codes, country codes, and locales](#supported-language-codes-country-codes-and-locales).

Corresponds to GIS admin0.

inputFields.name: streetAddress
inputFields.description:
Street address of the primary work location for the job. Include the street name and number.

**Example (USA)**: 1600 Pennsylvania Ave

**Example (Japan)**: 2-7-2

inputFields.name: cityRegionPostal
inputFields.description:
City and administrative region for your country, such as state, county, or prefecture, and postal code.

**Example (USA)**: Washington, District of Columbia, 20500

**Example (Japan)**: 100-8994 東京都千代田区丸の内

**Example (UK)**: Mayfair, London, W1J

inputFields.name: jobSource
inputFields.description: Information about the source of the job, whether a company, agency, franchise, and so on.

inputFields.name: jobPostingId
inputFields.description:
A unique identifier for the job within the applicant tracking system (ATS). Historically, this value is known as the _reference number_.

If defining seats in `SourcedJobPostingBodyInput.seats`, the individual
`SourcedJobPostingSeatInput.seatPostingId` values will be each job posts' _reference number_.
When defining a job with seats, `jobPostingId` is a grouping of one or more seats that become
individual job posts in Indeed.

inputFields.name: jobRequisitionId
inputFields.description: Requisition ID for the job in your applicant tracking system (ATS). This value does not need to be unique.

inputFields.name: evergreenRequisitionId
inputFields.description: Evergreen requisition ID for the job in your ATS. Use this value when there are multiple job postings over time for the same job.

inputFields.name: talentPoolId
inputFields.description: Talent pool ID. Use this value to track the talent pool applications to which this job should be tagged.

inputFields.name: taxonomyClassification
inputFields.description: Classification of the job within Indeed.

inputFields.name: datePublished
inputFields.description:
Date when this job was, or is to be, first published.

For some use cases, this could be in the future. If so, this represents when the job
will be "published" and available through <https://indeed.com> or other API endpoints.

**DO NOT** set this in the future, unless Indeed has communicated that a client's jobs
are eligible for delayed publishing. If Indeed has **NOT** communicated this, and the `publishDate`
is in the future, the job will not become available on <https://indeed.com> or other API endpoints.

**Note:** If your site publishes the publication date, this date must match the date on your site.

inputFields.name: url
inputFields.description: URL for this job posting on your site. Use the URL for the job description page, not the application page. Include the `source=Indeed` token URL parameter to track clicks from Indeed.

inputFields.name: numberOfHires
inputFields.description:
Number of people to be hired for this job posting.

If the number of people to be hired is unknown, leave this `null`. Do not specify a value.

If the number if people to be hired is undecided, but may be known in the future, specify `-1`.

inputFields.name: expirationDate
inputFields.description:
Date when hiring expires for this posting.

If provided and not changed by a future request, the job can be removed from Indeed.

inputFields.name: photoUrl
inputFields.description:
Photos for this job.

Deprecated. Use the `photos` field.

inputFields.name: photos
inputFields.description: Photos for the job.

inputFields.name: contacts
inputFields.description:
User and contact information for the job.

Must include exactly one contact with a `contactType` that includes `contact`.

inputFields.name: studentMetadata
inputFields.description:
Metadata that defines aspects of jobs that are for college/university students
and recent graduates.

The existence of a non-null value indicates that this is a job posting for an
internship, soon to be graduated, or recently graduated students.

inputFields.name: applicationDueDate
inputFields.description:
The date when applications are due.

This date is inclusive. If `2024-08-01` is specified,
then applications are accepted all day on `2024-08-01`.

inputFields.name: billingId
inputFields.description: Identifier for use by clients internally to help identify their own business units

inputFields.name: visibility
inputFields.description: Metadata that determines visibility of the job posting across Indeed search and other job surfaces.

inputFields.name: trackingUrl
inputFields.description: A URL that is triggered when a job is viewed, enabling external analytics for job views.

inputFields.name: photoUrl
inputFields.description: URL of the photo associated with the job.

inputFields.name: probationaryConditions
inputFields.description:
Text description of the probationary period. Add here the detail on working conditions (e.g. salary,
working hours, employment types) during the probationary period if it is different from one after the probation.

inputFields.name: probationaryTime
inputFields.description:
Length of time of the probationary period.

Include full details in the `probationaryConditions` field. The API ignores this field.
inputFields.deprecationReason: Include full details in the `probationaryConditions` field. This field is ignored.

inputFields.name: probationarySalary
inputFields.description: Salary information for the probationary period.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingSalaryInput
types.description:
Input object of structured salary information for the job. Use the minor currency units for your locale.

In the US, cents is the most minor unit.

In Japan, Yen is the most minor unit.

Use `maximumMinor` and `minimumMinor` to express a salary range.

If your salary is fixed, set both `maximumMinor` and `minimumMinor` to the same value. If your salary has a minimum, set only `minimumMinor`.

The `currency` field uses [ISO-4217 codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217#Active_codes_(List_One)). For example, `USD` or `JPY`.

The `salaryFrequency` field accepts hour, day, week, month, mile, or year.

inputFields.name: maximumMinor
inputFields.description: Maximum amount in the local minor currency.

inputFields.name: minimumMinor
inputFields.description: Minimum amount in the local minor currency.

inputFields.name: period
inputFields.description:
Period to pay.

This value also applies to other fields within this input object. For example, if `period == MONTHLY`, then working
hours under `fineGrainedSalaryInformation` are the expected number of working hours per month.

To ensure your job appears on Indeed, one of the following values is recommended:
* `DAY`
* `HOUR`
* `MILE`
* `MONTH`
* `WEEK`
* `YEAR`
* `TASK`
* `SHIFT`

Note: If `TASK` is selected, field `taskBasedSalaryInformation` must also be provided.

inputFields.name: fineGrainedSalaryInformation
inputFields.description: Additional information related to the salary for the job.

inputFields.name: taskBasedSalaryInformation
inputFields.description: Additional information related to the task for the job.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingScheduleDateRangeInput
types.description:
The date range for which a schedule tied to a shift starts and ends. Many jobs have
a known start date, while the end date is not defined. That is, a job with a start date that
will continue as long as the employer and worker decide to continue.

The dates should be the day where the first and last shift begin. For example, a shift
with a single day of work that crosses midnight should have the same `startDate` and
`endDate`. It should be the date the shift begins.

inputFields.name: startDate
inputFields.description: The first day a shift with this schedule begins.

inputFields.name: endDate
inputFields.description:
The last day a shift with this schedule ends. If this schedule repeats indefinitely,
do not provide a value. This value is inclusive - a endDate of `2025-01-05` indicates
the final working shift begins on `2025-01-05`, even if the final shift *ends* the following day.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingScheduleInput
types.description:
Schedule input for defining more fine-grained constraints on a seat.

As Indeed adds new functionality to increase relevant applies, based on jobseeker availability
and a job's schedule, more fields may be added to enable finer-grained scheduling definitions.

inputFields.name: dateRange
inputFields.description:
Define constraints in the job's availability with this field.

To define a start date

If a seat is not hiring for indefinite employment - consider seasonal or contract-based
employment - the period(s) in which the job is available may be defined here.

Date ranges are not required to be sequential without gaps.

inputFields.name: shifts
inputFields.description:
Definition of the shifts involved with this seat.

This is a place to define both specific shifts and schedule for a role, or to more generally
define the shifts a worker may be asked to work.

For job postings with a single shift on a single day, there should be one shift with a
schedule that begins and ends on the same day.

inputFields.name: timeZone
inputFields.description:
A timezone is required to rationalize shift times with a schedule.

If a job is worked across time zones, use the timezone in which the working
hours and schedule is defined.

For example, if a worker clocks-in for work in St. Louis, MO, but also performs
work on the Illinois side of the St. Louis metro-area, you should specify
the time zone for Missouri, and not that for Illinois.

To respect local Daylight Savings Time periods, the proper canonical time zone must
be specified. For example, if I set a timezone as an offset for Chicago, IL, as
`UTC-06:00`, this is only correct during winter months. The offset from UTC is constant.
If the timezone should support Daylight Savings Time for Chicago, IL, "America/Chicago" must
be specified.
NOTE: "America/Chicago" is the proper timezone for any DST consideration in the so-called
US Central Timezone.

inputFields.name: seatPostingId
inputFields.description:
A unique identifier for the seat in an application tracking system, or external client systems.

When posting a job with multiple seats and/or locations, a client must provide a unique
identifier for the seat. The `seatPostingId` must be unique across all
`SourcedJobPostingSeatInput` entities in a `createSourcedJobPostings` request. Otherwise,
the API will return a `BAD_USER_INPUT` error.

For future requests to update a job, given any `sourceName` and `jobPostingId` combination,
seats and their locations are created or expired, depending on if the `seatPostingId` is
new, or has been removed from the `seats` list, respectively.

`seatPostingId` have 250 characters or fewer.

**Important note when defining a `CreateSourcedJobPostingInput` object with
`SourcedJobPostingSeatInput` objects**:
    In Indeed systems, reports, analytics, or APIs that refer to a job posting's
    so-called `referencenumber` or `referenceId`, the value specified for `seatPostingId` is
    the job posting's `referencenumber`.

inputFields.name: seatLocation
inputFields.description:
The location where the work for this seat will be done.

For jobs with multiple seats in multiple locations, all locations MUST be in the same country.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingShiftsInput
types.description:
A shift is defined with as little as the working hours for a single shift. More detailed
information would include the schedule for a shift. i.e. what days are the shift on,
and when does this schedule end. For example, if modeling a job with a single shift,
a schedule should state the start and end date as the same `Date`. If modeling a shift
that repeats indefinitely, a schedule should have no end date.

inputFields.name: shiftTimes
inputFields.description:
The time periods for a shift. If defining shift information, there must be at least
one time schedule defined. Details for any breaks during the shift will be defined in
this object.

inputFields.name: schedule
inputFields.description:
Optionally define a schedule for this shift time period.

A schedule is not necessary for defining shifts for a seat.

Additional constraints may be described in the job description.

inputFields.name: notes
inputFields.description:
Optional notes including what to wear, what to bring, location details, or anything
else that a worker must know or do when working this shift.

inputFields.name: workTime
inputFields.description: The time period a hired worker is expected to work this shift.

inputFields.name: breakPeriod
inputFields.description: Information related to breaks during this shift.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingStudentMetadataInput
types.description:
Metadata that defines aspects of jobs that are for college/university students
and recent graduates.

inputFields.name: startMonth
inputFields.description:
The month the internship starts.

If the internship has multiple options in which it may start, specify each month.

If there are no requirements for when the job starts, or it is unknown, specify an empty list.

inputFields.name: period
inputFields.description:
Length of the internship, using the date portion of ISO8601. That is, `P[n]Y[n]M[n]W[n]D`, without
any hours, minutes, or seconds specified.

When specifying months or years, for the purposes of searching for jobs and
range validation:

| **Unit** | **Days** |
|----------|----------|
| 1 Month  | 30       |
| 1 Year   | 365      |

If weeks are specified (P2W), it is normalized to days (P14D), and that will be the output.
Otherwise, the same input is maintained, even with the internal conversion for search and validation purposes.

Examples:

| **Input** | **Output** | **Days** |
|-----------|------------|----------|
| P1M30D    | P1M30D     | 60       |
| P2M       | P2M        | 60       |
| P2W       | P14D       | 14       |
| P1M2W3D   | P1M17D     | 47       |

inputFields.name: graduationYear

inputFields.name: programType
inputFields.description:
The type of internship program.

* OpenCompanyProgram: A shorter, 1-3 day, engagement to learn more about a company.
* InternshipProgram: A longer, at least approximately one month, engagement where the candidate performs specific work for a company.

inputFields.name: previousYearHires
inputFields.description:
The number of people the company hired for the same role or occupation in the previous year.

This field is a legal requirement for New Grad jobs in the Japanese market,
and should be provided as an integer.
The value represents the total count of hires made for equivalent positions in the year
prior to this job posting.

If not provided for Japanese New Grad jobs, the job may not appear on Indeed.

This field is only applicable to New Grad jobs and should not be populated for other
types of student jobs. It is not necessary for any jobs outside of Japan.

Use one of the following strings to best describe this role's location flexibility.

* **Fully Remote**. Job can be performed remotely. No on-site work is required.

types.name: SourcedJobPostingTimeRangeInput
types.description:
The time range of a shift, based on the start time of a shift and the duration
up to the end time of a shift. The duration should not have any break time subtracted
from it.

A duration allows modeling for shifts longer than 24 hours, while a DateTime value does
not make sense for a shift that repeats.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description:
The local start time for a work period. When a TimeZone is required for calculations,

inputFields.name: durationToEndTime
inputFields.description:
The duration of the shift. This should not exceed 29 hours. For calculations that
require an end time, `duration` is added to `startTime`.

This SHOULD NOT have break time subtracted from the total shift duration.
If the shift is from 08:00 to 17:00, with a one hour break, the specified value should be `P9H`

The currency to apply to this budget and all budgets for the authenticated
Employer account. An employer's currency can be locked for various reasons,
including location, whether they have active jobs or active/inactive billing,
so providing a different currency for employer's with locked currencies will
be considered a bad input.

inputFields.description: This sets the end date of the budget, must be in ISO-8601 format. Example: 2019-01-13T06:00:00Z

inputFields.name: maxCpc
inputFields.description: This defines the max cost per click. This can only be set when plan is LIFETIME.

inputFields.name: plan

LIFETIME define the period for which the amount will be spent.

`StructuredLocation` of type `CITY` with the code `Austin`, its parent would be a `StructuredLocation` of type `ADMIN1` with the code

inputFields.name: maxWeight
inputFields.description:
maxWeight is ONE measure of the 'capacity' of this period. The weight for a period is the sum of all weights of appointments occurring during that time range.

Appointments can be booked for this period only while the period weight (including the new appointment) is less than or equal to the maxWeight.

In most cases, this value should be thought of as the number of humans conducting this interview. For 1:1 cases, this value should be 1.0 since there is only one human. For back-to-back cases where there could be multiple humans conducting appointments concurrently, this value could be > 1.0.

This value is NOT meant to be the same as an RSVP Cap. Please reach out to the S&A team if you have any questions.

The maxWeight must be greater than 0.0. This value will only be used for Include Periods and should not be set on Exclude Periods.

types.name: TaskRun
types.description:
Represents a complete task execution including all retry attempts.

A TaskRun is the top-level entity that tracks a task from submission to completion.
It contains multiple TaskRunAttempts if retries are configured, and provides
the overall status and configuration for the entire task execution.

Use Cases:
- Submit long-running data processing jobs
- Execute model training or batch inference tasks
- Run maintenance scripts across multiple environments
- Orchestrate complex multi-step workflows

Key Fields to Monitor:
- `status`: Overall task completion status
- `runAttempts`: Detailed history of all execution attempts
- `retryStrategy`: Complete retry configuration including count and timeouts

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for this task. Use this ID to query task status and details.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Current overall status of the task across all attempts. Check this to see if your task succeeded or failed.

fields.name: retryStrategy
fields.description: Retry strategy configuration for this task execution including retry count and timeout settings

fields.name: runAttempts
fields.description: Complete history of execution attempts for this task, ordered chronologically. Most recent attempt is last.

fields.name: taskConfig
fields.description: Runtime-specific configuration used to execute this task. Contains engine-specific parameters and settings.

fields.name: originatingRequestId
fields.description: ID of the request that originated this task. Null for direct task submissions, populated with backfill ID for tasks created by backfill requests.

fields.name: assetId
fields.description: ID of the asset that was used to create this task via runAsset mutation. Null for direct task runs created via runTask mutation.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this task was originally submitted to the system

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this task was last updated (status change, new attempt, etc.)

types.name: TaskRunAttempt
types.description:
Represents a single execution attempt of a task in a runtime environment.

Each time a task runs (initial execution + retries), a new TaskRunAttempt is created.
This provides detailed information about what happened during that specific execution,
including external system details, timing, and failure reasons.

Debugging Tips:
- Check `failureReason` for error details when status is FAILED
- Use `externalRunURL` to view logs and details in the runtime system
- Compare `startedAt` and `endedAt` to understand execution duration

fields.name: id
fields.description: Unique identifier for this specific execution attempt

fields.name: taskId
fields.description: ID of the parent task that this attempt belongs to

fields.name: status
fields.description: Status of this specific attempt (may differ from overall task status)

fields.name: externalRunId
fields.description: External system identifier for this execution (e.g., Kubernetes Job ID, Step Function execution ARN)

fields.name: externalRunUrl
fields.description: Direct URL to monitor this execution in the external system (e.g., Kubernetes dashboard, AWS console)

fields.name: logUrl
fields.description: Convenience link to logs for this attempt (engine-specific construction)

fields.name: latestMessage
fields.description: Latest message from the run service for this attempt. May contain status information, error details, or other relevant messages.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this attempt began execution in the external system

fields.name: endedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this attempt completed (successfully or unsuccessfully)

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this attempt record was created in our system

types.name: TaskStatus
types.description:
Task execution status indicating the current state of a task or run attempt.

Status Flow:
PENDING → RUNNING → [SUCCEEDED | FAILED | TIMED_OUT | CANCELED]

- Use SUCCEEDED/FAILED to check if your task completed successfully
- TIMED_OUT indicates the task exceeded its configured timeout
- CANCELED means the task was manually stopped (if supported)

enumValues.name: PENDING
enumValues.description: Task has been created but not yet started execution

enumValues.name: RUNNING
enumValues.description: Task is currently executing in the runtime environment

enumValues.name: FAILED
enumValues.description: Task execution failed due to an error or exception

enumValues.name: SUCCEEDED
enumValues.description: Task completed successfully with expected results

enumValues.name: CANCELED
enumValues.description: Task was manually canceled before completion

enumValues.name: CANCELING
enumValues.description: Task cancellation is in progress

enumValues.name: TIMED_OUT
enumValues.description: Task exceeded its maximum allowed execution time

enumValues.name: UNKNOWN
enumValues.description: Task status could not be determined (system error)

the metrics computed without dimensions. This type encapsulates the title,
description, metrics, data, and insights for the total metrics report.

making it suitable for summary statistics or KPI displays.

types.name: TotalAnalyticsMetricsInput
types.description:
Defines the input parameters for retrieving total analytics metrics data.
This input type allows consumers to specify which metrics report to retrieve
and how to filter the data. Unlike grouped metrics, total metrics are computed
without dimensions, making them suitable for summary statistics or KPI displays
that show overall values across the entire dataset.

inputFields.name: id

The unique identifier of the metrics report to retrieve.
This determines which predefined set of metrics will be available
in the response, such as "performance-funnel" or other report types.

inputFields.name: filter
inputFields.description:
Filtering criteria to apply to the metrics data.
This field is required and must include at least a dateRange to specify
the time period for which metrics should be calculated.
Additional field filters can be applied to narrow the dataset
before calculating the total metrics.

types.name: UpdateCampaignBudgetInput
types.description: The budget input for updating a campaign.

inputFields.name: recurringUnit
inputFields.description:
Defines the recurring duration of the budget.
For example if it’s monthly then the total budget is refreshed monthly by the limit amount.
Must be defined.

inputFields.name: prorationBehavior
inputFields.description:
Defines the proration behavior for budget updates during recurring periods.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations if unifiedProrationOptIn is true
- Defaults to START_NOW_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets if not specified, during budget type change
- Changing this value will trigger a proration resetting and prorated budget recalculation

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* cleared value when recurringUnit is Lifetime/AvgDaily.

inputFields.name: lastMonthProrationBehavior
inputFields.description:
Determines whether the budget for the last month should be prorated or use the full amount.

Important notes:
- Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
- The value is only considered when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled (true)
- Last provided value persists for future budget recalculations when unifiedProrationOptIn is enabled
- When a campaign's first and last month are the same, prorationBehavior setting takes precedence
- Works in conjunction with the general prorationBehavior setting
- Controls budget allocation specifically for the campaign's final month
- If not specified, defaults to LAST_MONTH_FULL_AMOUNT for monthly budgets, during budget type change
- Changing this value will trigger prorated budget recalculation during the campaign's final month

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* cleared value when recurringUnit is Lifetime/AvgDaily.

inputFields.name: limit
inputFields.description: The budget amount for the duration of the recurring unit. Must be defined.

inputFields.name: prorationOptions
inputFields.description: update settings that control budget proration behavior during campaign lifecycle.

types.name: UpdateCampaignLegacyObjectiveInput
types.description:
The input for updating campaign objectives in the legacy format used by enterprise clients.
Objectives provide additional structure to creating Campaigns,
providing the ability to tailor Campaigns to specific Objectives based on required hiring goals.

Only CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED can be changed to any other CampaignLegacyObjectiveType

inputFields.name: balance
inputFields.description:
Set to true to update CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to BALANCE
Balances the budget across all jobs within the Campaign. This aims to deliver as many applications as possible.

inputFields.name: budget
inputFields.description:
Set to true to update CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to BUDGET
Does not balance budget across jobs. This may result in some jobs using the majority of the budget.
Delivers as many applications as possible but will favor some jobs over others.

inputFields.name: quick
inputFields.description:
Set to true to update CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to QUICK
An experimental objective, which enables results to be delivered as quickly as possible.

inputFields.name: interview
inputFields.description:
Set a specific number of interviews to target for the jobs within a campaign.
This can be set to the same number for all jobs, or tailored for unique jobs.
When the target number of interviews is hit, spend on these jobs will be significantly reduced and allocated elsewhere.

Updates CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to INTERVIEW if not already

inputFields.name: targetApplies
inputFields.description:
Set a specific number of applications to target for the jobs within a campaign.
This can be set to the same number for all jobs, or tailored for unique jobs.
When the target number of applications is hit, spend on these jobs will be significantly reduced and allocated elsewhere.

Updates CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to TARGET_APPLIES if not already

inputFields.name: tcpa
inputFields.description:
Target Cost Per Application.
The Campaign will aim to achieve the selected Cost Per Apply price across the Campaign.

Updates CampaignLegacyObjectiveType UNSPECIFIED to TCPA if not already

types.name: UpdateCampaignProrationOptionsInput
types.description: Update settings that control budget proration behavior during campaign lifecycle..

inputFields.name: resetProrationOnBudgetChange
inputFields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during updates.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for prorated budget calculation unless explicitly modified
- Required budget change to new value during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates. Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
Defaults to FIRST_MONTH_ONLY, unless explicitly set during budget type change.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* cleared value when recurringUnit is Lifetime/AvgDaily.

inputFields.name: resetProrationOnReactivation
inputFields.description:
Reset Proration Period & calculated the prorated budget amount as First Month Proration during campaign reactivation.

When enabled:
- Resets the proration period to the first month of the campaign
- Uses the last provided proration behavior for recalculation unless explicitly modified
- Requires status change to ACTIVE during update for this to take effect
- Last passed value persists for future prorated budget recalculations

This configuration can be modified during subsequent updates. Only applicable for monthly recurring budgets
Defaults to NEVER, unless explicitly set during budget type change.

refer: https://indeed.atlassian.net/wiki/x/DQE1Kg

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* reset to false value when recurringUnit is Lifetime/AvgDaily.

types.description: The schedule input for updating a Campaign.

inputFields.name: startDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become active. This field affects
the budget by the prorationBehavior field.
Optional, campaign is paused if it has no startDate.
Updating the startDateTime will trigger reproration based on the existing proration behavior at that point in time for the AdGroup Platform Budget.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

inputFields.name: endDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should become inactive. This field affects
the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

Setting both the endDateTime and targetEndDateTime is unsupported and may result in unspecified behavior.
In addition, targetEndDateTime cannot be used with MONTHLY recurring budget.

inputFields.name: targetEndDateTime
inputFields.description:
When the campaign should optimize for the desired outcome.
Campaign is allowed to continue to spend past this date.
This field affects the spending behavior by interacting with the DeliveryObjective.
Can be none. Cannot be set at the same time when endDate is also set.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

Setting both the endDateTime and targetEndDateTime is unsupported and may result in unspecified behavior.
In addition, targetEndDateTime cannot be used with MONTHLY recurring budget.

inputFields.name: extEndDateTime
inputFields.description:
This field captures the user-specified external end date for the campaign.
When set, this represents the date and time when the campaign should end based on campaign type requirements.
Can be none if the campaign is open ended.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

An RFC-3339 encoded date time string with zero offset (e.g., "2023-12-31T23:59:59Z").

Note: Setting the endDateTime or targetEndDateTime is not supported when extEndDateTime is set.
These fields are mutually exclusive. This is only supported for hosted monthly and daily campaigns.
