Legacy campaign keys historically used by different indeed surfaces.
This field is primarily meant for backward compatibility. Clients should use id / rawId as the primary identifier of a campaign.

Note: Only one out of id, rawId, legacyKey can be used for update.

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description:
Human friendly name of the campaign.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: status
inputFields.description:
Status to be updated.

If nothing is passed then, Campaign will be retain existing status.

inputFields.name: unlinkHostedJobBudget
inputFields.description:
If configured to 'true', the platform will allow new hosted campaigns to be created for the employer job ID
which is already associated with this campaign, thereby unlinking the current budget from the job.

inputFields.name: deliveryObjective
inputFields.description:
The primary objective of the campaign.
Each campaign must have one primary objective.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Only one input among deliveryObjective and legacyObjective can be specified

inputFields.name: legacyObjective
inputFields.description:
The objective of the campaign in the legacy format used by enterprise clients.
This cannot be used alongside delivery objective in the input.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Only one input among deliveryObjective and legacyObjective can be specified

inputFields.name: optInChannels
inputFields.description:
List of channels to enable

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: optOutChannels
inputFields.description:
List of channels to disable.
Applied after optInChannels.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: schedule
inputFields.description:
A value object that defines the campaign schedule to
specify the start and end datetime of the campaign.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: budget
inputFields.description:
The overall budget the campaign is allowed to charge.
Can be calculated from the objective if using a fixed per-outcome pricing model.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: createAdGroups
inputFields.description:
List of AdGroups to create

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: updateAdGroups
inputFields.description:
List of AdGroups to update

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: idempotencyKey
inputFields.description:
Allow retrying requests without performing the same operation twice.

Client must supply a unique value generated by the client. We suggest
using V4 UUIDs, or another random string with enough entropy.

Keys guarantee up to 24 hours of idempotency. After that same key can be
used again.

Note: we haven't really talked about the guarantee & implementation around
idempotency so please consider the key and the doc a placeholder.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: false
* Value is nullable: false

inputFields.name: preferredBackend
inputFields.description: DEPRECATED: Nothing happens if this is set.

inputFields.name: experimental
inputFields.description: A namespace for experimental campaign properties.

inputFields.name: trackingToken
inputFields.description:
The click tracking token appended to the job URL on sponsored clicks.
Allows the employer to identify that the click is from Indeed,
and if desired, the campaign that sponsored the click.

- maxLength: 255
- minLength: 0
- example: `&source=indeed`

inputFields.name: extRefId
inputFields.description:
A unique reference id, an employer can set to their campaign.
Allows you to reference a campaign with an external system id.
If the updated extRefId already exists for an Employer then campaign update fails.

- maxLength: 60
- minLength: 0
- example: `2345678-90ab-cdef-1234-567890abcdef`

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: jobConfigs
inputFields.description:
Operations for Updating job configs associated with the campaign

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: false
* Omitted in input means no change.

inputFields.name: package
inputFields.description:
Update Package details linked to the Campaign

Input Semantics:

inputFields.name: contract
inputFields.description:
Update contract details linked to the campaign.

Input Semantics:

* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

inputFields.name: adGroup

Update Package details linked to the Campaign

Input Semantics:

* null and absent are ignored

inputFields.name: sponsorshipTier
inputFields.description:
Sponsorship tier of the campaign.

Input semantics:
* Input is optional: true
* Value is nullable: true
* Omitted in input means no change.
* Set to null to clear the value.

types.name: UpdateQuestionsAndAnswersInput
types.description:
Input for updating questions and answers in an application draft.

This input supports two mutually exclusive approaches:
1. Legacy approach: Use `screener` and `interviewScreener` fields (deprecated)
2. New approach: Use `questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput` field (recommended)

Validation Rules for Update Attempts:
Any attempt to update will result in an error if any of the following rules are violated:

- Cannot use both legacy fields (screener or interviewScreener) and questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput at the same time.
- When using questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput, each section name (questionsAndAnswersSectionName) must be unique within the list; duplicate section names are not allowed.
- When using questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput, updates are permitted only for sections that already exist in the draft.
- When using questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput, only section types that are supported can be updated.

For questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput:
- Supports updating multiple question sections in a single mutation
- Each section type can appear only once
- Empty or null question lists (questionsAndAnswersSection list in the questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput object) within sections are ignored
- Only questions that exist in the original draft and are provided in the input will be updated
- Supported section types
    - SCREENER_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - DEMOGRAPHIC_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - INTERVIEW_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - INDEED_QUALIFICATION_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS

Legacy fields (screener/interviewScreener) will be deprecated in favor of questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput.

inputFields.name: applicationDraftId
inputFields.description: Application draft id. It must be a valid UUID.

inputFields.name: screener
inputFields.description:
Questions IDs and corresponding answers for screener questions
screener will be replaced by questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput. New clients should use questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput
TODO: Mark screener as deprecated and nullabe in IASUB-2178

inputFields.name: interviewScreener
inputFields.description:
Questions IDs and corresponding answers for interview screener questions
interviewScreener will be replaced by questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput. New clients should use questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput
TODO: Mark interviewScreener as deprecated and nullabe in IASUB-2178

inputFields.name: questionsAndAnswersSectionsInput
inputFields.description:
Supports updating multiple question sections.
Supported section types
    - SCREENER_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - DEMOGRAPHIC_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - INTERVIEW_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
    - INDEED_QUALIFICATION_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS
Use this field in favor of the screener and interviewScreener fields above that will be deprecated

Example (USA): Washington, District of Columbia, 20500
Example (UK): Mayfair, London, W1J

Example (USA): 1600 Pennsylvania Ave

If specified, the weekly availability rules will be divided and returned in periods of the
given size. The periods will align the highest [StartInterval] that is less than or equal to
the duration. Resulting periods that are less than the given duration are not
returned.

For example, if the calendar has the following availability rules
`WED 11:15-12:00`, `WED 12:00-13:10`, `THU 09:01-09:31`.
If the duration is set to 30 minutes, the following rules will be
returned: `WED 11:30-12:00`, `WED 12:00-12:30`, `WED 12:30-13:00`.
If the duration is set to 40 minutes, the following periods will be returned:
`WED 11:30-12:10`, `WED 12:30-13:10`.

The value has a resolution of 1 minute. Minimum value is 1 minute.

types.name: WorkedShiftMutations
types.description: Mutations for the WorkedShift entity and related types

fields.name: clockIn
fields.description: Upsert a single WorkedShift with the given clock in time

fields.name: clockOut
fields.description: Upsert a single WorkedShift with the given clock out time

fields.name: endMeal
fields.description:
End an active meal on an WorkedShift with the given end time
Mutation will error if:
- meal overlaps with existing meals
- meal ends after WorkedShift clock out (if already clocked out)
- meal does not exist on this WorkedShift

fields.name: updateTimeDetails
fields.description:
Upsert multiple WorkedShifts with the given times and/or break duration
Can create fully clocked WorkedShifts, or update multiple fields at once
Performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, they all fail and will be rolled back

fields.name: startMeal
fields.description:
Add a single meal onto an active WorkedShift with the given start time
Mutation will error if:
- meal overlaps with existing meals
- start is before WorkedShift clock in time
- WorkedShift is already ended (instead, use addMeals mutation)

fields.name: addMeals
fields.description:
Add multiple meals onto multiple WorkedShifts with the given start and end times
If the meal overlaps with other inputs or existing meals or is not confined with the
WorkedShift clock in and out times, mutation will error
Performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, they all fail and will be rolled back

fields.name: updateMeals
fields.description:
Update multiple meals on multiple WorkedShifts with the given optional times
If a meal overlaps with other inputs or existing meals or is not confined with the
WorkedShift clock in and out times, mutation will error
If a meal doesn't exist on the WorkedShift, mutation will error
Performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, they all fail and will be rolled back

fields.name: deleteMeals
fields.description:
Delete multiple meals from WorkedShifts, effectively replacing it with normal worked time
Deleting a meal will not change the overall duration of the WorkedShift
If a meal doesn't exist on its WorkedShift, mutation will no-op
Performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, they all fail and will be rolled back
Will only delete the WorkedShiftMeal for the given subject, so deleting may not affect the underlying queried data
e.g. if WorkedShift WORKER meal exists & WorkedShift CLIENT meal does not, deleting WorkedShift CLIENT meal will no-op
and querying for WorkedShift CLIENT will still return WorkedShift WORKER data

fields.name: approve
fields.description:
Mark multiple WorkedShifts as approved and resolve flags if WORKER
Not performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, others may have succeeded
If the WorkedShift for the given subject does not exist but the WorkedShift
for the 'other' subject does exist, this will clone that WorkedShift for this
subject and approve
If any WorkedShift does not exist for either subject, updates must be included as well

fields.name: unapprove
fields.description:
Mark multiple WorkedShifts as unapproved
If any WorkedShift does not exist for the given subject, mutation will error
WorkedShift for a subject must first explicitly exist before it can be unapproved

fields.name: delete
fields.description:
Delete all data associated with multiple WorkedShifts and resolve flags if WORKER
Not performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, others may have succeeded
Will only delete the WorkedShift for the given subject, so deleting may not affect the underlying queried data
e.g. if WorkedShift WORKER exists & WorkedShift CLIENT does not, deleting WorkedShift CLIENT will no-op
and querying for WorkedShift CLIENT will still return WorkedShift WORKER data

fields.name: undelete
fields.description:
Restore all data associated with WorkedShifts
If a WorkedShift is not deleted, the action will no-op and that WorkedShift will be returned as is
This mutation has specific errors distinguished by the `code` and `subcode` fields within the `extensions` field in the `errors` array:
- {code: BAD_USER_INPUT, subcode: INVALID_UNDELETED_WORKED_SHIFT}: state of the WorkedShift data overlaps with previous deleted data or otherwise is incongruent when restored
- {code: BAD_USER_INPUT, subcode: NOT_FOUND}: a WorkedShift could not be resolved, the item in the payload list will be null and the errors' `path` field will point to that respective index
Performed in bulk in a transaction. If any fails, they all fail and will be rolled back

fields.name: flag
fields.description:
Mark a WorkedShift as flagged for review, indicating that the WorkedShift is untrustworthy
and must be reviewed internally before approval. Flagged WorkedShifts are not eligible for instant pay.
Only supports flagging WORKER WorkedShifts, since CLIENT WorkedShifts do not require review
If any WorkedShift does not exist for either subject, mutation will error
Re-flagging will not error, only upsert the list of reasons
If the reasons argument is empty, all old reasons will be marked as false and the WorkedShift will be unflagged.

Currently only supports flagging one WorkedShift (input ids is a list to support future expansion)

fields.name: resolveFlags
fields.description:
Resolve flagged WorkedShifts, indicating that the WorkedShift can now be considered trustworthy
Only supports resolving WORKER WorkedShifts, since only WORKER WorkedShifts can be flagged
Options:
- Resolve as WORKER, meaning the flagged WorkedShift can be considered trustworthy as is,
  so we approve and unflag it
- Resolve as CLIENT, meaning the flagged WorkedShift is confirmed untrustworthy,
  so we overwrite it with CLIENT WorkedShift times, approve, and unflag it

Currently only supports resolving one WorkedShift (input ids is a list to support future expansion)

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.
